Therefore, one should give up anger and control like a charioteer, one’s senses, running forth towards their objects like very wicked horses, after turning them away from their objects (17—23)
m.uttara.p2.26: “A man should do good to the people around himself by thought, by action and by speech. He should not hurt anybody. No sin, therefore, will attach to him. The harm, which is wrought by evil thoughts, are not done by a sharp sword or a serpent trampled by foot or an ever wrothful enemy. One who has learnt discipline, even his temperament cannot be changed. Even if someone conceals his evil nature, it is surely betrayed by his action. (24—26)
m.uttara.p2.27: Thus asked by Śrī Rāma, who was unwearied in actions, the Brāhmaṇa Sarvārthasiddha said this in Śrī Rāma’s presence: (27)
m.uttara.p2.29: ‘While I was going about for begging food the appropriate time for begging had passed, I was overpowered by anger, so I beat it. The dog, which was standing on the road (blocking my way) was asked by me to move away. Not moving at all, it stood in the middle of the road in an odd manner. (28-29)
m.uttara.p2.31: ‘Overtaken by hunger, O Rāma! I beat it angrily. O King of kings! Punish me, a guilty person, O chief of kings! Having been punished by you, I would not be afraid of hell.’ Thereafter Śrī Rāma asked all the members of the assembly, ‘What should be done to him, and what punishment should be meted out to him? For, if proper punishment is given to the guilty, the subjects are protected.’ (30-31)
m.uttara.p2.34: Bhṛgu, Aṅgirā, Kutsa and others, Vasiṣṭha alongwith Kāśyapa, eminent teachers of laws, ministers and interpreters of the Vedas—these and many other scholars were present there. All of them—the masters of scriptures and those who were well-versed in state-affairs told Śrī Rāma that a Brāhmaṇa is not to be awarded capital punishment, it is declared by experts in scriptures. (32—34)
m.uttara.p2.36: Then all the hermits addressed Śrī Rāma in following words, “A King holds sway over everyone. O Śrī Rāma! Specially You, who is the eternal god Viṣṇu, are the ruler of the three worlds.” (35-36)
m.uttara.p2.39: When all of them had addressed thus, the dog said as follows: “If you are pleased with me, O Rāma, and if you are to bestow on me a boon, then listen to me, O Valiant One! You asked me what you should do for me, and promised (to do what I would request you to do). So make him O King! a ‘Kulapati’ as promised by you. Your Majesty! make him ‘Kulapati’ of Kālanjara.” On hearing this Śrī Rāma consecrated him as a Kulapati. (37—39)
m.uttara.p2.46: Thus honoured, the happy Brāhmaṇa went away riding on elephant-back. Then the ministers smilingly with astonishment, said to Śrī Rāma, “He has been given a boon. O resplendent one. This is not a curse.” Thus told by the ministers Śrī Rāma said: “You do not know the truth about the course of actions. The dog knows the reason (and will tell why the Brāhmaṇa has been made Kulapati).” On being asked thus by Śrī Rāma, the dog addressed the following speech: “I, In my previous birth, was the Kulapati of the same place, Kālañjara Maṭha. Partaking of the remains of sacrificial food, O Rāma ! I would be engaged in worshipping gods and Brāhmaṇas and gave to the male and maid-servants their due. I had a love for good things. I would protect the property dedicated to gods. I was modest and well-behaved and was engaged in doing good to all living beings. Even then I have been reduced to this wretched state and the lowest position. O Rāma! therefore such a Brāhmaṇa, who is irasible, who has given up his ‘Dharma’ and who is engaged in harming others, who is hot-tempered, ruthless, harsh, foolish (ignorant) and irreligious will lead to the downfall of fourteen generations. (40—46)
m.uttara.p2.52: “Therefore, one should not in any circumstances become a Kulapati. Only, he should be made to look after gods, cows and the Brāhmaṇas, whom one would wish to condemn to go to hell alongwith sons, cattle and relatives. One who takes away the property of the Brāhmaṇas, gods, women and children and takes back again what has been given away in charity, perishes alongwith one’s all dear ones. O Śrī Rāma! One who takes away the property belonging to the Brāhmaṇas and the gods, soon goes to the fearful hell known as ‘Avīci’ one who takes away even mentally the property belonging to the gods and the Brāhmaṇas, goes down from one hell to another.” On hearing the speech of the dog, the eyes of Śrī Rāma opened widely due to wonder, the dog, too possessed of lustre, went to place from where it had come. It was a high minded soul in its former birth but on being born as a dog it has been spoiled. The illustrious one sought death by abstaining from taking food in Vārāṇasī. (47—52)
m.uttara.60.1: Thus, as the day passed by with Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa conversing among themselves, the vernal night appeared, which was neither cold nor hot. (1)
m.uttara.60.2: After dawn in the morning, which was a clear one, having performed the morning duties, Śrī Rāma the scion of Kākutstha approached the place where he could see his subjects, desirous to know the activities of the citizens. (2)
m.uttara.60.3: Then Sumantra, the charioteer, having come near Śrī Rāma, the scion of Raghus, spoke thus: ‘O King ! Some ascetics, not permited to enter, stand in need at the entrance door, (3)
m.uttara.60.10: ‘O Tiger among men, Śrī Rāma, great Ṛṣis, who dwell at the banks of the Yamunā, and rejoice among themselves, placing Cyavana, the Bhārgava (son of Bhṛgu) at their head, implore us in haste for your audience’. Hearing him say so, Śrī Rāma the righteous one spoke: ‘Please let the Brāhmaṇas, headed by Bhārgava, enter.’ The charioteer then went near the door. Accepting the orders of the King, made the ascetics, who were unapproachable, enter: More than a hundred holy ascetics, glowing with their own lustre, entered the palace. Those Brāhmaṇas accompanied with pitchers full and sanctified with the waters of all the Tīrthas (pilgrimages), and with many fruits and roots offered them to Śrī Rāma. Accepting them, Śrī Rāma was pleased excessively getting the sacred waters of the Tīrthas and all kinds of fruits, He, Śrī Rāma, of long arms, then addressed all the great ascetics thus: (4—10)
m.uttara.60.12: “These are the special seats, please be seated as it sults you”. Hearing the words of Śrī Rāma all the great Ṛṣis seated themselves on the lovely golden cushions. Seeing them thus seated, the conqueror of the strongholds of enemies, the scion of the Raghus, serenly with joined hands uttered these words: (11-12)
m.uttara.60.13: ‘For what purpose do you come here, what should I perform for you. I am at your command. I shall happily perform all that is desired by you. (13)
m.uttara.60.14: ‘This kingdom, my entire life, and even what dwells in my heart, all that is for the Brāhmaṇas, I speak to you the truth’. (14)
m.uttara.60.16: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma and His prolonged proclamation, the Ṛṣis, who were performing right penances and dwelling on the banks of the Yamunā, arose. In great joy the noble ones said: ‘O best among men, this befits you alone in this world, and none other. (15-16)
m.uttara.60.17: ‘Many powerful kings have gone by, who looking at the greatness of our task, never desired to promise to fulfil them. (17)
m.uttara.60.18: ‘Respecting Brāhmaṇas you made promise, without having a second thought about the task. No doubt, therefore you will dispell all fears that haunt Ṛṣis.’ (18)
m.uttara.61.1: As the Ṛṣis spoke thus, Śrī Rāma the scion of Kakutstha said: ‘O ascetics, speak out the task that I should perform, so as your fear may be dispelled’. (1)
m.uttara.61.2: When the scion of Kakutstha spoke these words, Bhārgava replied: ‘O best among men! hark ! what causes fear to us and the country. (2)
m.uttara.61.3: ‘Formerly, in the Kṛtayuga, O king ! In Kṛtayuga, Madhu from the Daitya clan, the wise and great Asura was the eldest son of Lolā. (3)
m.uttara.61.4: “He was respectful to Brāhmaṇas and was also a source of refuge and well-composed of mind. His relations with the very gracious gods were incomparably cordial. (4)
m.uttara.61.5: “That Madhu, although possessed of might, was well-established in the path of righteousness; and was given by Rudra, Mahādeva, a wonderful boon, because of his respect for the Devas. (5)
m.uttara.61.6: “The great Mahādeva produced a most powerful and luminous trident from his own trident, being excessively pleased, gave it to him and said these words: (6)
m.uttara.61.7: “By your unparalleled right conduct, you have earned my pleasure: so highly pleased, I give you this excellent weapon. (7)
m.uttara.61.8: “As long as you do not oppose the Brāhmaṇas and the gods (Devas), this trident of yours will retain its power, otherwise it will perish. (8)
m.uttara.61.9: “Whosoever fearlessly encounters you in battle, the trident will reduce him to ashes and return to your hand.” (9)
m.uttara.61.10: “Thus having obtained the boon from Lord Śiva, the great Asura on his part made obeisance to Mahādeva and also said: (10)
m.uttara.61.11: ‘O Lord, may this unparalleled trident, belong to my race forever. O God, You are the Lord of the all dieties.’ (11)
m.uttara.61.12: The Mahādeva, Śiva, the Lord of all, replied to Madhu, ‘This cannot be so. (12)
m.uttara.61.13: “Though the sentence uttered by me out of pleasure, however, will not go in vain for you: this trident will belong to one of your sons. (13)
m.uttara.61.14: “As long as this trident will remain in the hand of your son, he will be unassailable by all beings.” (14)
m.uttara.61.15: “Thus having obtained the great and wonderful boon from Mahādeva, Madhu, the greatest among the Asuras, got a palace full of brilliance built. (15)
m.uttara.61.16: ‘His dear wife, the famous beautiful Kumbhīnasī, the daughter of Viśvāvasu, was born from Analā. (16)
m.uttara.61.17: ‘Her son, the powerful and cruel one, Lavaṇa by name, was wicked since childhood and performed only evil deeds. (17)
m.uttara.61.18: ‘Seeing this son so wicked, Madhu was enraged and grieved, but did not say to him anything. (18)
m.uttara.61.19: ‘He entered the ocean, leaving this world, handing over the trident to Lavaṇa and conveying him the power of the boon. (19)
m.uttara.61.20: “He (Lavaṇa) by the power of the trident and with his wickedness, caused much trouble to the three worlds, especially the ascetics. (20)
m.uttara.61.21: ‘So mighty is Lavaṇa and such is the trident. O scion of Kakutstha. Now you have heard; so it is up to you to do what is necessary, you are our ultimate resort. (21)
m.uttara.61.22: ‘Formerly many kings, O powerful one, were approached for protection by the Ṛṣis frightened, but we did not find any protector. (22)
m.uttara.61.23: ‘So now, having heard of Rāvaṇa killed alongwith his army, O dear one, we do not consider any other king on this earth as protector, and thus we desire protection for those who are persecuted by Lavaṇa. (23)
m.uttara.61.24: ‘Thus, we have conveyed to you, O Rāma of unfailing power, that fear and cause of that fear. We know, you can ward off that; do something.’ (24)
m.uttara.62.1: When the Ṛṣis had thus spoken to Him, Śrī Rāma with folded hands replied: ‘What does he (Lavaṇa) take as his food, of what conduct is he and where does he stay?’ (1)
m.uttara.62.2: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma, all those Ṛṣis then conveyed to Him how Lavaṇa fared. (2)
m.uttara.62.3: His food comprises all beings, specially ascetics. His conduct is full of cruelty, every moment. His residence is in Madhuvana. (3)
m.uttara.62.4: Having killed many thousands of lions, tigers, deers and birds and also human beings, he makes his daily meals of them. (4)
m.uttara.62.5: Then all other types of beings too, the mighty Lavaṇa devoures as if he was Death, with open mouth at the time. (5)
m.uttara.62.6: Hearing this, the scion of Raghu (Śrī Rāma) said to the great ascetics: ‘I shall kill that Rākṣasa, may your fears be dispelled.’ (6)
m.uttara.62.7: Thus having promised to the ascetics, possessed of great vigour, that descendant of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, spoke to his brothers altogether. (7)
m.uttara.62.8: “Who the brave shall kill Lavaṇa, to whom shall Lavaṇa be assigned, to long-armed Bharata or Śatrughna, the wise one?’ (8)
m.uttara.62.9: When Śrī Rāma spoke thus, Bharata said: ‘I shall kill him. Kindly assign him to me’. (9)
m.uttara.62.11: Hearing the words of Bharata, (Śatrughna) younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa, stood up leaving his golden seat. Having bowed to the King, Śrī Rāma, Śatrughna said: The middle one, Bharata, among us, possessed of long arms, O descendant of Raghu, has already performed his share. (10-11)
m.uttara.62.12: ‘He protected Ayodhyā in your absence undergoing so much mental agony, awaiting your arrival. (12)
m.uttara.62.14: ‘Here many sufferings were endured by him, O king: sleeping on uncomfortable bed in the Nandigrāma, this noble one consuming only fruits and roots, with matted hair, and dress of bark, has greatly experienced sorrow, O descendant of the Raghus. (13-14)
m.uttara.62.15: ‘While I, the servant, am available, Bharata should not again be put to trouble. After Śatrughna said so, Śrī Rāma, the scion of the Raghus again spoke these words: (15)
m.uttara.62.20: “Be it so, O Śatrughna (descendant of Kakutstha), carry out my orders, I shall consecrate you on the holy kingdom of Madhu. Establish the throne. Bharata be here. O one of long arms, if you consider it proper, You are brave and proficient, and also have the ability to establish a new city. Founding a city close to Yamunā, and many provinces of auspicious fame, one who having reduced a royal house in that very city, does not install a king there, indeed goes to hell. Therefore, you, having killed Lavaṇa, the son of Madhu, possessed of evil designs, rule over that kingdom. If you follow my words, then, O brave one, carry on the administration righteously, without making any argument or disobeying me.’ (16—20)
m.uttara.62.21: The elders must be obeyed by youngers there is no doubt about it. Please approve of the consecration, to be performed by me, accompained by the Mantras, sacred chants of the Brāhmaṇas headed by Śrī Vasiṣṭha, in prescribed manner. (21)
m.uttara.63.1: After Śrī Rāma said so, the mighty Śatrughna felt very much ashamed and spoke gently: (1)
m.uttara.63.2: ‘O king, the descendent of Kakutstha, this transaction seems to me as against Dharma, how can a junior be consecrated on the throne, superseding the elders? (2)
m.uttara.63.3: ‘On the other hand, your orders must be carried out at any cost as it is impossible to supersede them. (3)
m.uttara.63.4: ‘I have heard from you, as well as from the Śrutis, O brave one! that I should not have said anything after the middle brother, Bharata, had already taken a vow. (4)
m.uttara.63.5: ‘It is most unfortunate that I have said something improper: ‘I will kill Lavaṇa in battle’. I think I have been put in this unenviable position as a result of my saying so. (5)
m.uttara.63.7: ‘When the elder one says something, the younger should not make a reply. Violation would be against the norms of Dharma and spoil the other world. Therefore, O Kakutstha, I will not speak anything again. O giver of respect, may I not be importuned for the punishment second time. (6-7)
m.uttara.63.8: ‘O king, the best among persons and delighter of Raghus, I will follow your wishes but whatever wrongful happens in it from me, you please destroy it. I shall act according to your desire, O bull among men. Please leave out for my sake that which is unlawful, O scion of Kakutstha, descendant of the Raghus!’ (8)
m.uttara.63.9: After these words being uttered by the wise and the brave Śatrughna, Śrī Rāma was pleased and He spoke to Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa: (9)
m.uttara.63.10: ‘Bring forth all the requisites of consecration, this very day. I shall consecrate the scion of the Raghus, the tiger among men, Śatrughna. (10)
m.uttara.63.11: ‘By my orders, call all of them, the chief priest, Vasiṣṭha, the townsmen, and other priests and also the councillors.’ (11)
m.uttara.63.12: Following the orders of the king, the great warriors, brought the necessary pūjā materials for the consecration, making the chief priest Vasiṣṭha play the prominent role. (12)
m.uttara.63.13: The Kings and the Brāhmaṇas entered the royal palace; thus the consecration of the noble Śatrughna went on. (13)
m.uttara.63.18: The venerable scion of Kakutstha, when consecrated, shown as the sun and brought great joy to the descendant of Raghu (Rāma) and also to the citizens, as Skanda (Kārtikeya) when consecrated in the old days by the gods together with Indra. As Śatrughna was consecrated by Śrī Rāma, the citizens were happy and so also the learned Brāhmaṇas. Kausalyā, Sumitrā, Kaikeyī and all other king mothers performed auspicious acts in the royal palace. The noble Ṛṣis dwelling on the banks of the Yamunā were confident that Lavaṇa was as if dead due to the consecration of Śatrughna. Then the scion of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, placing Śatrughna on His lap uttered these sweet words enhancing his power. (14—18)
m.uttara.63.19: ‘I give you this divine arrow, which is unfailing and conquers the foes, O descendant of Raghu. O handsome one, you will kill Lavaṇa with this arrow. (19)
m.uttara.63.20: ‘This arrow was created O scion of Kakutstha, when the self-born unconquerable God, Viṣṇu, was reclining in the great ocean, whom the gods and the demons could not see. (20)
m.uttara.63.23: ‘Therefore, this one, the best among arrows, is invisible to all beings, this was created by angry Viṣṇu, desirous of the destruction of the two wicked ones, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, and creation of the three worlds after the two and the other Rākṣasas were killed with this arrow. (21—23)
m.uttara.63.24: ‘This arrow was not shot by me formerly even to kill Rāvaṇa (the king of the Rākṣasas), O Śatrughna, for that would have caused the great destruction of other beings too. (24)
m.uttara.63.26: ‘The great trident, the best among weapons, that was given to Madhu by the mighty three-eyed Lord Śiva for the purpose of destroying the foes; placing that honourable weapon at home, Lavaṇa proceeding to all quarters repeatedly acquires the best of his food. (25-26)
m.uttara.63.27: ‘Whenever, desirous of struggle one per chance challanges him, then the Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, taking hold of this trident reduces him indeed to ashes. (27)
m.uttara.63.28: ‘So you, O lion among men, accompanied with the weapon (arrow), stay at the eastern gate, and fight with him, dispossessed of the weapon (trident) and unable to enter the city. (28)
m.uttara.63.29: ‘O one of long arms ! Challenge him to fight before he has entered his residence; then you shall kill the Rākṣasa. (29)
m.uttara.63.30: ‘If it is not so done, then, indeed, he will be unassailable, but if this is so done, then, O brave one, Lavaṇa will be destroyed. (30)
m.uttara.63.31: ‘Thus, all has been narrated to you, and also the warding off of the trident, the doings of the blue-throated Śiva are indeed difficult to overcome.’ (31)
m.uttara.64.1: Having thus spoken to the scion of Kakutstha and eulogizing him again and again, the descendant of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, spoke again to him: (1)
m.uttara.64.3: ‘These four thousand of horses, two thousand chariots and a hundred of the best elephants, the rows of stalls (inside the city), laden with goods for sale and purchase, may follow you O Śatrughna, the scion of Kakutstha and so also the actors and dancers. O Śatrughna, O bull among men, having taken a lac of pure gold-coins well-equipped with wealth and carriers (elephants and horses), you proceed to Madhurā. (2-3)
m.uttara.64.5: ‘O brave one, keep the army that is well-formed, in such good cheer that its constituents are happy and satisfied, and not arrogant, with your good words. (4-5)
m.uttara.64.6: ‘There (at the encounter) neither wealth nor spouse, nor even relatives are at your side, as the servants when kept happy. (6)
m.uttara.64.7: ‘Thus, having dispatched the mighty army full of happy men, you alone, with bow in your hand, can go to the forest of Madhu. (7)
m.uttara.64.8: ‘You should go in a manner in which the son of Madhu, Lavaṇa does not know that you are going to him for an encounter. (8)
m.uttara.64.9: ‘O bull among men, there is indeed no other way in which Lavaṇa would die, whosoever goes to attack him, is killed by Lavaṇa, indeed. (9)
m.uttara.64.10: ‘Thus when summer is passed, and the rainy season comes, you should kill Lavaṇa. O graceful one, that is the time of death for this wicked one. (10)
m.uttara.64.11: ‘Your warriors may proceed with the great Ṛṣis at their head, so that by the end of the summer season, they may cross the Gaṅgā, the daughter of Jāhnu. (11)
m.uttara.64.12: ‘Then having stationed your army at the banks there, O one of speedy steps, you go ahead carefully alone with the bow.’ (12)
m.uttara.64.13: Thus being spoken to by Śrī Rāma, Śatrughna, having gathered together the brave chiefs of the army spoke thus to them: (13)
m.uttara.64.14: ‘These are the decided places where you can dwell, according to your liking; wherever you are stay amicably.’ (14)
m.uttara.64.15: Thus ordering them and despatching the mighty army, he made obeisance to Kausalyā, Sumitrā and Kaikeyī. (15)
m.uttara.64.17: Paying salutation to Śrī Rāma with his head and going round Him, and falling at the feet of Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, and the chief priest Vasiṣṭha, Śatrughna of pious mind, the torturer of the foes, the mighty one going round Śrī Rāma again, departed. (16-17)
m.uttara.64.18: Sending ahead the army then, full of elephants and horses, he himself lived there with Śrī Rāma for a month and then he too started. (18)
m.uttara.65.1: Despatching the entire army, residing for a month only in Ayodhyā on his way, Śatrughna alone proceeded in haste. (1)
m.uttara.65.2: After spending two nights on the way, Śatrughna, descendant of the Raghus, reached the holy hermitage of Vālmīki, the best of the places to dwell. (2)
m.uttara.65.3: Śatrughna after saluting him with folded hands spoke these words to Vālmīki, the best among the ascetics: (3)
m.uttara.65.4: ‘Sir, I desire to stay here; I have come for a mighty purpose. I shall go tomorrow morning to the west, the quarter of Varuṇa.’ (4)
m.uttara.65.5: Having heard those words of Śatrughna, the best among the ascetics, Vālmīki, said cheerfully to him (Śatrughna), the noble one: “Welcome to thee, O famous one. (5)
m.uttara.65.6: “O gracious one, this hermitage is indeed your own, the family of the descendants of Raghu. Accept without hesitation the Pādya (ablutions of the foot), Arghya and the seat offered by me.” (6)
m.uttara.65.7: Accepting then the homage and the fruits and the roots, the scion of Kakutstha, took the food and was fully satisfied. (7)
m.uttara.65.8: Having taken the fruits and the roots, he (Śatrughna) said to that great Ṛṣi: ‘To whom belong all these accoutrements of sacrifice that are seen on the eastern side, close to the hermitage’ (8)
m.uttara.65.9: Hearing these words of Śatrughna, Vālmīki spoke out: “O Śatrughna! listen as to whom this place of sacrifice belonged formerly. (9)
m.uttara.65.10: “Among your ancestors there was Saudāsa, and of that king, was a son named Vīrasaha, who was very brave and extremely pious. (10)
m.uttara.65.11: “Although young, yet valiant Saudāsa went out for hunting in forest and saw two Rākṣasas roaming about. (11)
m.uttara.65.12: “Those two Rākṣasas assuming the dreadful shape of the lion and devouring many thousands of animals, yet they were still unsatiated. (12)
m.uttara.65.13: “Seeing those two Rākṣasas and the forest devoid of animals, he, Saudāsa, was enraged and killed one of them with a mighty shaft. (13)
m.uttara.65.14: “Having killed one of the Rākṣasas the bull among men, Saudāsa, without worry and anger looked at the slain Rākṣasa. (14)
m.uttara.65.16: “Having seen the dead Rākṣasa, his comrade was greatly pained and said to Saudāsa: ‘As you have killed that Rākṣasa, a friend of mine, who was not at all guilty, so O sinful one, I shall take my revenge on you.” (15-16)
m.uttara.65.17: Having said so, that Rākṣasa disappeared. After the lapse of some time, Mitrasaha (Vīrasaha) became the king of Ayodhyā. (17)
m.uttara.65.18: The king also performed the great sacrifice, the Aśvamedha (horse-sacrifice) near the hermitage and Vasiṣṭha also participated in that sacrifice. (18)
m.uttara.65.19: The great sacrifice lasted for many years and was comparable with the sacrifice of the gods being performed with great pomp. (19)
m.uttara.65.20: Now at the end of this sacrifice, the Rākṣasa in the form of Vasiṣṭha remembering the former enmity spoke to the king. (20)
m.uttara.65.21: ‘At the conclusion of the last part of the sacrifice, give me immediately my food consisting of flesh, and do not ponder over this.’ (21)
m.uttara.65.22: Hearing those words, spoken by Rākṣasa in the form of Brāhmaṇa Vasiṣṭha, the king spoke to the expert cooks: (22)
m.uttara.65.23: ‘Prepare soon such food possessed of flesh, fatty and worthy of offering, so that our preceptor, Vasiṣṭha, is satisfied.’ (23)
m.uttara.65.24: The chief of the cooks was perturbed in mind at the orders of the king; then that Rākṣasa soon took the form of the cook. (24)
m.uttara.65.25: He brought human flesh to the king and said: “This tasteful food, possessed of flesh, has been brought by me.’ (25)
m.uttara.65.26: That best among men (Vīrasaha) together with his wife Madayantī offered this food possessed of flesh brought by the Rākṣasa to Vasiṣṭha. (26)
m.uttara.65.28: Knowing human flesh to have been brought as food, the Brāhmaṇa (Vasiṣṭha) possessed of great anger ventured to speak thus: ‘O king as you desire to give such food to me, so no doubt this shall be your food’. (27-28)
m.uttara.65.29: Then Saudāsa enraged by this, took up a hand-full of water and was on the point of cursing Vasiṣṭha; his wife, however, checked him. (29)
m.uttara.65.30: ‘As the holy Ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha is our venerable preceptor and a chief priest comparable to the gods, O king! so you cannot curse him in return.’ (30)
m.uttara.65.31: Then the pious Saudāsa employed the water held in his hand, which was infused with anger and his spiritual power and sprinkled his feet with it. (31)
m.uttara.65.33: By it (this sprinkling) the feet of the king became variegated in colour, and thence the king by name Saudāsa, became famous as Kalmāṣapāda (with feet of dark-variegated colour), and was so known. That King with his wife falling at the feet of Vasiṣṭha again and again repeated to Vasiṣṭha what was uttered by the Rākṣasa, in the form of a Brāhmaṇa. (32-33)
m.uttara.65.34: After having heard what the King said and knowing the food being contaminated by the Rākṣasa, Vasiṣṭḥa again spoke to Saudāsa, the bull among men: (34)
m.uttara.65.35: ‘These words that have been uttered by me in anger, cannot be rendered ineffective, I will, however, grant you a boon. (35)
m.uttara.65.36: The curse will come to an end after twelve years and by my grace, you will not remember the past.” (36)
m.uttara.65.37: Thus that King, the extirpator of enemies, having borne that curse, regained his kingdom and protected his subjects. (37)
m.uttara.65.38: ‘Of that Kalmāṣapāda is this holy place of sacrifice, near the hermitage about which you asked me’. (38)
m.uttara.65.39: Having heard this dreadful story of that king Kalmāṣapāda, Śatrughna saluted the great Ṛṣi and entered the hutment. (39)
m.uttara.66.1: During that night Śatrughna entered the arbour. The same very night Sītā gave birth to two sons. (1)
m.uttara.66.2: At midnight, the young ascetics spoke to sage Vālmīki about the auspicious motherhood of Sītā, which news very much pleased him: (2)
m.uttara.66.3: ‘Sir, the wife of Rāma has given birth to two sons. So, O powerful one, make the protecting rites that destroy the ill spirits of the nether world.’ (3)
m.uttara.66.4: Hearing these words from them, the great sage went there and saw the two sons, who were like sons of the gods and were as effulgent as the moon. (4)
m.uttara.66.5: The sage went there joyfully and looked at the two sons and made the sacrament for both of them that kills the inauspicous Bhūtas and destroys the Rākṣasa. (5)
m.uttara.66.6: That Brāhmaṇa Vālmīki took the handful of Kuśa and Lava (the lower portion of the Kuśa grass) and preparing the totemic device, handed it over to them, the protective symbol that kills the Bhūtas. (6)
m.uttara.66.7: ‘He who of the two was born first should be cleansed with the Kuśas purified by chants and then his name will be ‘Kuśa.’ (7)
m.uttara.66.8: ‘Who happens to be born later, should be cleansed carefully with Lava by the old women and will be known by the name of Lava. (8)
m.uttara.66.9: ‘Thus these twins named Kuśa and Lava will become famous bearing the names given by me.’ (9)
m.uttara.66.10: Then the old women of Āśrama pure in mind took with care the totemic device from the hands of the sage and performed the protective rites of the twins. (10)
m.uttara.66.12: While in this manner (the symbolic protection) was being performed by the old women, Śatrughna at midnight heard the joyful Gotra and name of Śrī Rāma and also the news of delivery of the two sons by Sītā and then having entered the arbour of Sītā said, ‘O mother, by the grace of God two sons are born to you.’ (11-12)
m.uttara.66.13: Then the night of the rainy season of the month of Śrāvaṇa (full moon) passed swiftly with noble Śatrughna enjoying himself. (13)
m.uttara.66.14: At break of dawn, having performed the morning ablutions, he (Śatrughna) taking leave of the sage with folded hands, started forth to the western direction. (14)
m.uttara.66.15: Reaching the banks of the Yamunā, and having spent seven nights on the way he (Śatrughna) made for his stay in the hermitages of the sages of holy fame. (15)
m.uttara.66.16: He, the famous one, dwelt there with the sages among whom Bhārgava was the foremost, taking part in talks proper to the occasion. (16)
m.uttara.66.17: This way the mightiest among Raghus and great souled Śatrughna in the company of sages like Cyavana passed that night through hearing various religious tales. (17)
m.uttara.67.2: Then as the night appeared, Śatrughna asked the Brāhmaṇa, Cyavana, son of Bhṛgu the exact might of Lavaṇa, and the power of the trident also. He enquired, ‘O Brāhmaṇa, who were killed by this special trident having entered into a duel with Lavaṇa.’ (1-2)
m.uttara.67.3: Hearing these words of the noble Śatrughna, the mighty Cyavana said in reply to the scion of the Raghus: (3)
m.uttara.67.4: ‘Among the innumerable doings of this Lavaṇa listen to me that which took place in the context of the originator of the family of Ikṣvāku (Māndhātā). (4)
m.uttara.67.5: ‘In the old days, there was a powerful king, the son of Yuvanāśva, known as Māndhātā, noted for his might in the three worlds. (5)
m.uttara.67.6: ‘Having ruled over the entire earth, that king, lord of the earth, embarked on a conquest of the world of the gods from here, the earth. (6)
m.uttara.67.7: ‘Great fear overcame Indra and other mighty gods, when Māndhātā prepared to fight with a desire to conquer the world of gods. (7)
m.uttara.67.8: Propitiated by the host of gods, Māndhātā, the king, having vowed to take one half of Indra’s kingdom and the other half of earthly sovereignty, went up to raid heaven. (8)
m.uttara.67.9: ‘Indra, the conqueror of Pāka Daitya, having known his evil intentions, uttered these conciliatory words to the progeny of Yuvanāśva. (9)
m.uttara.67.10: ‘O bull among men, Māndhātā, you are still not established as a king in the mortal worlds, and you desire the kingdom of the gods here without subjugating the earth. (10)
m.uttara.67.11: ‘O brave one, if the entire earth is indeed under your sway then you may rule over the kingdom of the gods together with your attendants, army and carriers. (11)
m.uttara.67.12: Māndhātā said to Indra: ‘O Indra, where does my rule over the earth is obstructed’? (12)
m.uttara.67.13: The thousand-eyed Indra told him, ‘O sinless one, the son of Madhu, the Rākṣasa Lavaṇa by name, does not obey your orders.’ (13)
m.uttara.67.14: Having heard the dreadful unpleasant words, conveyed by Indra, the King put to shame with face downcast, could not speak. (14)
m.uttara.67.15: Taking leave of the thousand-eyed god, with his face turned somewhat downwards, the lord of the mortals proceeded and came back again to this world. (15)
m.uttara.67.16: That king, the destroyer of foes, with anger in his heart and together with his attendants and carriers came to bring the son of Madhu, Lavaṇa, under his sway. (16)
m.uttara.67.17: Desirous to fight with Lavaṇa, the bull among men, Māndhātā, sent a messenger to Lavaṇa. (17)
m.uttara.67.18: He, the messenger, having approached the son of Madhu, said many unpleasant words; the Rākṣasa devoured that messenger while he was speaking thus. (18)
m.uttara.67.19: The messenger, on being late in returning, the King possessed of anger, inflicted injury on the Rākṣasa by shower of arrows on all sides. (19)
m.uttara.67.20: Then that Rākṣasa laughed and took the trident in his hand and released the best among weapons, the trident, for the purpose of slaying Māndhātā with all his followers. (20)
m.uttara.67.21: That enflamed trident on its part, having rendered to ashes the king together with his attendant, army and carriers—came back to the hand of Lavaṇa. (21)
m.uttara.67.22: Thus that great King was killed together with his army and carriers, O gracious one, the power of the trident is impossible to fathom. (22)
m.uttara.67.23: Tomorrow morning, you shall soon kill Lavaṇa while he is without the weapon, there is no doubt that your victory is certain. (23)
m.uttara.67.25: By you performing this deed the welfare of the worlds will be achieved. Thus all has been narrated to you, O bull among men, about the might of the wicked Lavaṇa and the unfathomable dreadful power of the trident, O king Māndhātā; Lavaṇa perished due to his own misdeeds. (24-25)
m.uttara.67.26: Tomorrow morning you will slay Lavaṇa I have no doubt, O noble one, when he will proceed for flesh, having not the trident with him, victory shall be yours, O king of men. (26)
m.uttara.68.1: The night passed away quickly while staying at the hermitage of Cyavana, the noble Śatrughna conversing with Cyavana and other sages, who wished for his holy victory (against Lavaṇa). (1)
m.uttara.68.2: Then in the morning when it was dawn, that Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, the heroic one, went out of his city impelled by the desire to bring his food. (2)
m.uttara.68.3: In the meantime, Śatrughna, the brave one, having crossed the Yamunā, stood at the gates of the city of Madhu, with bow in his hand. (3)
m.uttara.68.4: Then at midday that Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, the evil-doer returned bearing the load of many thousand creatures. (4)
m.uttara.68.5: Then the Rākṣasa saw Śatrughna armed with the bow, standing at the gate and said to him: ‘What will you do with this weapon? (5)
m.uttara.68.6: ‘Many thousands of men like you accompanied with weapons, O wretched one, have been devoured by me in anger. Death seems to have come nearer to you. (6)
m.uttara.68.7: ‘O vile one, my food is yet incomplete, having come, you enter my mouth of your own accord?’ (7)
m.uttara.68.8: While the Rākṣasa spoke thus and laughing, the heroic Śatrughna broke in tears with anger. (8)
m.uttara.68.9: Fiery rays issued forth from all the limbs of the noble and angry Śatrughna. (9)
m.uttara.68.10: Highly enraged, Śatrughna then addressed the demon, who roamed about thus at right, ‘O evil one, I wish to have a duel with you. (10)
m.uttara.68.11: ‘I am the son of (King) Daśaratha, and the brother of the wise Śrī Rāma, the extirpator of foes, Śatrughna by name. I have come with a desire to kill you. (11)
m.uttara.68.12: ‘So give the duel to me, who desires to fight with you! You are the enemy of all beings; with me alive here you shall not escape.’ (12)
m.uttara.68.13: When Śatrughna had spoken thus, that Rākṣasa, Lavaṇa, replied to the best among men, as if laughing: ‘O wicked one, it is my good luck that you have come within my reach. (13)
m.uttara.68.14: ‘O insensate one, the Rākṣasa Rāvaṇa the brother of my maternal aunt, was killed by Rāma for the sake of a woman. (14)
m.uttara.68.15: All I had forgiven, the destruction of the family of Rāvaṇa, and ignoring specially you. (15)
m.uttara.68.16: ‘But now all of you, that have been born or will be born and even you vile ones, will be swept away by me like straws. (16)
m.uttara.68.17: ‘I shall indeed give you a fight, who wish it, O fool of vicious intellect. Just wait for a moment, while I bring my weapon (trident). (17)
m.uttara.68.18: ‘I am going to be equipped with the weapon with which I desire to kill you.’ At this Śatrughna at once spoke out: ‘Where will you go as long as I am alive? (18)
m.uttara.68.19: ‘The enemy that has come of his own accord does not deserve to be set free by one disciplined in mind. Whoever with unsettled mind gives freedom to a foe to disappear, that weak-minded one indeed would be killed as a coward. (19)
m.uttara.68.20: ‘You, therefore, have a good look at this world of mortals, O wicked one! I shall carry you to Yama’s abode with many sharp arrows, O foe of the three worlds and also of Raghu’s family.’ (20)
m.uttara.69.1: Hearing these words of the noble Śatrughna, Lavaṇa became extremely angry and said: ‘Wait for a moment’. (1)
m.uttara.69.2: Rubbing his one hand with the other, and making a rattling sound with his teeth, Lavaṇa challenged the lion among Raghus many times. (2)
m.uttara.69.3: To that Lavaṇa of fearful appearance, speaking thus, Śatrughna, the killer of the enemies of the gods, said these words: (3)
m.uttara.69.4: ‘Śatrughna was not born, when others were conquered by you in battle, so go to the abode of Yama today, killed by my arrow. (4)
m.uttara.69.5: ‘O sinful one, may the sages too see you killed in encounter today, also the learned Brāhmaṇas, as the gods saw Rāvaṇa killed. (5)
m.uttara.69.6: ‘Today there will be peace indeed in the city and province, as you, the demon roaming about at night are slain by my arrow and lie prostrate on the ground and burnt. (6)
m.uttara.69.7: ‘Today, the arrow, whose fore-point resembles the thunderbolt, released by my hand, shall enter your heart as the ray of the sun enters in the lotus.’ (7)
m.uttara.69.8: Being thus spoken, Lavaṇa enraged with anger threw a mightly tree on the breast of Śatrughna; but Śatrughna cut it thousandfold with arrows. (8)
m.uttara.69.9: Thus seeing his action fruitless, the powerful Rākṣasa again taking hold of many trees hurled them at Śatrughna. (9)
m.uttara.69.10: The brave Śatrughna too, tore asunder each one coming upon him, by three or four arrows of flatterend ends. (10)
m.uttara.69.11: Thus, Śatrughna then possessed of great might, let loose a shower of arrows on the Rākṣasa; however, the Rākṣasa was not troubled. (11)
m.uttara.69.12: Then the powerful Lavaṇa laughed, and lifting a tree attacked the brave one, Śatrughna, on the head; Śatrughna went into a swoon with the bodily joints loosened. (12)
m.uttara.69.13: So, as the brave Śatrughna fell, long cries of ‘Hā’ emanated from the sages, the host of the gods, the Gandharvas and Apsarās (the celestial beings). (13)
m.uttara.69.14: Ignoring Śatrughna, fallen on the ground whom he took killed, the Rākṣasa did not enter his residence, although given time to do so. (14)
m.uttara.69.15: Nor even did he, Lavaṇa, take up the trident seeing him (Śatrughna) lying on the ground, and then considering him, Śatrughna, dead, carried again his provisions. (15)
m.uttara.69.16: Gaining consciousness in a moment, Śatrughna, adored by the sages, stood up and waited at the door of the city of Madhu, weapon in his hand. (16)
m.uttara.69.20: Then Śatrughna took hold of the arrow: the divine and excelling others, flaming with brilliance and filling the ten quarters with its brilliance, shaped like the thunderbolt in front, resembling the thunderbolt in speed, equalling Meru and Mandara mountains, flat shaped, invincible in all encounters, smeared with red sandal-like blood, beautiful as the winged bird, dreadful for the lord of the Dānavas and also the mountains, resembling as if the fire of destruction kindled at the time of final dissolution. Seeing it, all beings were very much frightened. (17—20)
m.uttara.69.21: The whole world, together with the Devas, Asuras and Gandharvas and the sages, was in discomfort and all approached Pitāmaha (Brahmā). (21)
m.uttara.69.22: They narrated to the god of the gods, Prapitāmaha Brahmā, the bewilderment of the gods with fear regarding the security of the worlds. (22)
m.uttara.69.23: ‘O lord ! is the destruction of the world at hand or has the end of the universe approached? O grand sire, never before has such a condition of the world been seen or heard.’ (23)
m.uttara.69.24: Hearing their words, Brahmā the grandfather of the worlds, protector of the gods, revealed the cause of the fear of the gods. (24)
m.uttara.69.25: He said in a sweet voice: ‘All the gods listen to me; the arrow has been held by Śatrughna for the slaying of Lavaṇa in encounter. (25)
m.uttara.69.28: ‘All the great gods are bewildered at the power of that arrow ! O my children, this is the eternal powerful arrow of the former God, the creator of the world, Viṣṇu, due to which the gods are in fear; this mighty arrow was created for the destruction of those two sons of Diti, Madhu and Kaiṭabha; Viṣṇu alone knows well about this powerful arrow. (26—28)
m.uttara.69.33: ‘This arrow is the ancient form of the noble Viṣṇu; go from here, O my children, and witness Lavaṇa being killed by the noble and heroic Śatrughna, the younger brother of Śrī Rāma.’ The gods hearing the words of the God of gods, came to the place where both Śatrughna and Lavaṇa were engaged in fighting; all beings witnessed that divine arrow borne by Śatrughna in his hand, as if it was the fire that broke out at the time of universal destruction. Seeing the sky filled with the gods, Śatrughna, again having roared like a loin, looked at Lavaṇa; he (Lavaṇa) was again challenged by the noble Śatrughna. (29—33)
m.uttara.69.36: Lavaṇa filled with anger appeared to give him (Śatrughna) the fight. He, Śatrughna, the best among archers, then having stretched that bow up to his ear, shot the arrow at the mighty chest of Lavaṇa. That divine arrow descended to the nether-world breaking open Lavaṇa’s chest, and having gone there, being worshipped by the gods, came back quickly again to Śatrughna, the descendant of the family of Ikṣvāku. (34—36)
m.uttara.69.37: That demon Lavaṇa being struck by the arrow of Śatrughna, fell on the ground all at once like the mountain struck by the thunderbolt. (37)
m.uttara.69.38: On the Rākṣasa Lavaṇa being killed, that mighty divine arrow too, came back to the quiver of Rudra as all the gods looked on. (38)
m.uttara.69.40: Then the champion of Raghus, Śatrughna, felled with one arrow the terror of three worlds, shone forth as the sun dispelling the darkness. All gods, sages, serpents paid homage to him and Apsarās hailed the fearless victory of the son of Śrī Daśaratha, the serpent laid to rest. (39-40)
m.uttara.70.1: After Lavaṇa was killed, the gods, together with Indra and Agni as their head, spoke these sweet words to Śatrughna, the tormentor of the foes. (1)
m.uttara.70.2: ‘O lion among men, by good fortune, victory is yours and the Rākṣasa is dead, O! of a noble vow! ask us for a boon. (2)
m.uttara.70.3: ‘All desirous of your victory are intending to grant boon to you. We have come; our presence here will not be fruitless.’ (3)
m.uttara.70.4: Hearing the words of the gods, Śatrughna, the long-armed one, disciplined in mind, keeping his folded hands on his head replied thus : (4)
m.uttara.70.5: ‘This city of Madhu, Madhurā by name, built by the gods, may become the capital soon. This is the only boon that I desire: (5)
m.uttara.70.6: The gods said: ‘So be it’ O scion of the Raghus: This beautiful city will be Śūrasenā indeed, possessed of an army of brave men, there is no doubt about it.’ (6)
m.uttara.70.7: Thus saying the holy gods then ascended to heaven. Śatrughna too, the powerful one, brought back the army from the banks of the Gaṅgā. (7)
m.uttara.70.8: That army came soon, hearing the news of the death of Lavaṇa at the hands of Śatrughna and commenced the establishment of the capital in the month of Śrāvaṇa (roughly corresponding to July-August). (8)
m.uttara.70.9: That holy country was established as the territory of the Śūrasenas, in the course of twelve years, as there was no cause for fear. (9)
m.uttara.70.10: The fields were full with grains, Indra (the rain-god) brought forth rain in time, the warriors, protected by Śatrughna, were free of disease. (10)
m.uttara.70.11: That city, shaped like the half-moon, beautified by the banks of the Yamunā, was also embellished with special mansions and quadrangular market-place. It was inhabited by the four Varṇas (castes) and abounded in all forms of merchandise and trade. (11)
m.uttara.70.13: The white mansion that was formerly built by Lavaṇa, Śatrughna further beautified with pictures of various colours, looking beautiful on all sides with rest-houses and Vihāras, and that city was adorned with human and celestial embellishments. (12-13)
m.uttara.70.15: The prosperous Śatrughna, the younger brother of Bharata, having seen the city, divine in appearance, filled with all forms of merchandise and inhabited by traders coming from various countries, was much pleased. (14-15)
m.uttara.70.16: Then at the commencement of the twelfth year, having established the city Madhurā, he thought ‘I shall see the feet of Śrī Rāma.’ (16)
m.uttara.70.17: Then establishing that city, resembling a celestial one, Śatrughna filling it with men of various types, the enhancer of Raghu’s family, considered it appropriate to see Śrī Rāma’s feet. (17)
m.uttara.71.1: Then in the twelfth year Śatrughna, followed by a few attendants and the army, desired to proceed to Ayodhyā, ruled over by Śrī Rāma. (1)
m.uttara.71.2: Then making the army-chiefs and the councillors to retreat, he (Śatrughna) proceeded riding on a special horse, accompanied by a hundred chariots. (2)
m.uttara.71.3: Śatrughna, the descendant of the Raghus, possessed of fame, halting at seven to eight places on the way, reached the hermitage of Vālmīki and dwelt there. (3)
m.uttara.71.4: Having paid obeisance at the feet of sage Vālmīki, the famous Śatrughna accepted ablutions, offerings and hospitality from the sage. (4)
m.uttara.71.5: The sage, Vālmīki, narrated to the noble Śatrughna sweet tales of various themes. (5)
m.uttara.71.6: Referring to the killing of Lavaṇa, the sage said: ‘By killing Lavaṇa, a difficult task has been accomplished by you. (6)
m.uttara.71.7: ‘O gracious one, of long-arms, many powerful kings, together with their army and carriers had been killed by Lavaṇa, when they came in encounter with him. (7)
m.uttara.71.8: ‘O Bull among men, that evil one has been killed by you with ease, and by your prowess, the fright of worlds due to him has been dispelled. (8)
m.uttara.71.9: ‘The dreadful killing of Rāvaṇa by Śrī Rāma was achieved with great effort; this great task of killing Lavaṇa was performed by you without effort. (9)
m.uttara.71.10: ‘On Lavaṇa being killed, the gods are highly pleased. This admirable deed for all beings and the world has been performed by you. (10)
m.uttara.71.11: ‘That encounter with Lavaṇa was indeed seen by me, as it ensued, while I was sitting in the assembly of Vāsava (Indra), O bull among men. (11)
m.uttara.71.12: ‘My heart too, O Śatrughna, is filled with joy; I shall smell the crown of your head as this is the highest course of affection.’ (12)
m.uttara.71.13: Thus saying and smelling the crown of the head of Śatrughna, the wise one, Vālmīki, offered hospitality to him and all those who followed him. (13)
m.uttara.71.15: That jewel among men, Śatrughna, took the food offered by Vālmīki; then heard the deeds of Śrī Rāma, as they were performed by Him at that time melodiously, accompanied with the sound of the lute with proper beats and the three musical tunes manifested at proper beats, and at proper places, in Sanskrit, and according to the rules of music and also with the beat of drums at proper intervals. (14-15)
m.uttara.71.16: Śatrughna heard the deeds of Śrī Rāma as they were performed formerly, those words (comprising the song) were true and narrated as per the deeds performed in sequence. (16)
m.uttara.71.17: Having heard the story duly sung, the lion among men, Śatrughna, with tears in his eyes, was rendered unconscious, and fell into a swoon immediately taking deep sighs repeatedly. (17)
m.uttara.71.19: Śatrughna heard the deeds sung as if they were performed in the present. The warriors, who followed him, on hearing the rich song, were overwhelmed and speechless, indeed, and exclaimed to each other—‘How wonderful it is’. (18-19)
m.uttara.71.20: ‘What is this, where are we, have we been in a dream, that thing, which we had seen formerly, we see again in the hermitage. (20)
m.uttara.71.21: ‘Do we hear in dream this beautifully composed song’ filled with great surprise, they said to Śatrughna: (21)
m.uttara.71.24: ‘Please ask Vālmīki, O best among men, who composed this song? Śatrughna on his part, told all the warriors filled with surprise: ‘Here I am not able to ask Vālmīki in this manner, many wonders exist here in this hermitage of the sage, it is not proper to go and question the great sage out of curiosity.’ Thus having spoken to the warriors, the scion of the Raghus then having saluted the great sage, started for his apartment. (22—24)
m.uttara.72.1: Śatrughna, a tiger among men, could not sleep in the night ruminating over the song of Rāma’s deeds, full of meaning. (1)
m.uttara.72.2: Night passed away for the noble Śatrughna quickly, hearing the melodious sound of the song accompanied with that of the Vīṇā (lute) with proper beats. (2)
m.uttara.72.3: After the night had ended, Śatrughna with folded hands said to Vālmīki, the best among sages, having performed the morning duties: (3)
m.uttara.72.4: ‘Sir, I wish to see Śrī Rāma, the scion of the Raghus, with your permission and also that of these sages, firmly adhering to their vowes.’ (4)
m.uttara.72.5: Thus talking, Vālmīki embraced Śatrughna, the extirpator of foes, the scion of the Raghus, and let him go. (5)
m.uttara.72.6: Saluting Vālmīki, the best among sages, he, Śatrughna, ascending the shining chariot, went on speedily to Ayodhyā, eager to see the scion of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma. (6)
m.uttara.72.7: The descendant of Ikṣvāku, the prosperous one, Śatrughna, reached the city, Ayodhyā, and entered the king’s palace where Śrī Rāma, the illustrious one, was. (7)
m.uttara.72.9: Seeing Śrī Rāma with a face like full moon, seated among the councillors like Indra among the gods, and as if enflamed with vigour, Śatrughna with folded hands spoke to resplendant one after saluting Him: (8-9)
m.uttara.72.10: ‘All that you ordered me to do, I have done; the evil Lavaṇa has been killed and the city, Madhupurī, has been reinstituted. (10)
m.uttara.72.11: ‘These twelve years I have spent without you. O king, I cannot now live afar, separated from you. (11)
m.uttara.72.12: ‘O scion of the Kakutsthas, possessed of unmitigated power, give me thy favour, I cannot live without you for long, like a child separated from its mother.’ (12)
m.uttara.72.13: Then the scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma, embraced him, Śatrughna, who spoke thus and said: ‘O brave one, do not lose heart, this does not become a Kṣatriya. (13)
m.uttara.72.14: ‘O descendant of Raghu, Śatrughna, the Kings staying away from their kingdom are not disheartened; the subjects are indeed to be protected as laid down among duties for the Kṣatriya. (14)
m.uttara.72.15: ‘O brave one, come from time to time again to Ayodhyā to see me. O best among men, you should go to your city, the city of Madhurā. (15)
m.uttara.72.16: ‘You indeed are dearer to me than my life, there is no doubt. But for you looking after your territory is indeed obligatory. (16)
m.uttara.72.17: ‘Therefore, O scion of the Kakutsthas, stay with me for seven nights and then you should proceed to Madhurā with attendants, army and carriers.’ (17)
m.uttara.72.18: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma, spoken rightfully and in accordance with his Dharma, Śatrughna in a depressed tone spoke ‘So be it.’ (18)
m.uttara.72.19: As desired by the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, Śatrughna, the mighty one, made himself ready to depart, having spent seven nights there. (19)
m.uttara.72.20: Taking leave of the noble Śrī Rāma of true valour, and also Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa, he ascended the marvellous chariot. (20)
m.uttara.72.21: Followed by the noble Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata on foot, for a long distance, Śatrughna sped in haste to the city, Madhupurī. (21)
m.uttara.73.1: Having despatched Śatrughna, the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, together with the two brothers lived happily and contented, ruling rightfully over his kingdom. (1)
m.uttara.73.2: Then after a few days an old Brāhmaṇa citizen of Ayodhyā, carrying his dead son’s body, appeared at the royal gate. (2)
m.uttara.73.4: Filled with affection and sorrow, and crying, pronounced these words (exclamations) repeatedly ‘O son ! O son ! What evil deed have I committed in my former birth that I should see my only son dead. (3-4)
m.uttara.73.5: ‘O son, you have met with death untimely, having not reached adolescence and being a child of merely five thousand days (less than fourteen years) which leads to my sorrow. (5)
m.uttara.73.6: ‘O son, I, alongwith your mother, shall meet with death in a few days, there is no doubt about it. (6)
m.uttara.73.7: ‘I do not remember having spoken untruth, nor, even ever having committed sinful acts with regard to all beings. (7)
m.uttara.73.8: ‘Due to what evil deed, my own son, although a child, has gone away to the abode of Yama, the son of Vivasvān, without having performed the paternal rites (our last rites). (8)
m.uttara.73.9: ‘I have neither seen nor heard of such untimely death, of immature type, in the territory of Śrī Rāma. (9)
m.uttara.73.10: ‘There is no doubt that there must have been some evil deed performed by Śrī Rāma due to which indeed death meets the children in his territory. (10)
m.uttara.73.11: ‘There is no fear of death for the children in other territories. So, O king, bring back to life this child, possessed by death. (11)
m.uttara.73.12: ‘At the very royal gate, I shall lay down my life with my wife, like an orphan, O Śrī Rāma; you be happy having committed the sin of killing a Brāhmaṇa. (12)
m.uttara.73.13: ‘You will attain longlife with your brothers: till now we have lived happily in your kingdom, O mighty one. (13)
m.uttara.73.14: ‘This death of my son has befallen on me. Therefore, O Śrī Rāma, staying under you we are under the sway of death, and there is little chance of happiness now. (14)
m.uttara.73.15: ‘Presently the reign of the noble Ikṣvākus is rendered orphan; now having accepted Śrī Rāma as the master, in whose reign certainly children’s death will occur. (15)
m.uttara.73.16: ‘The subjects, who are not protected rightfully, perish on account of the faults of the kings; when the king is not rightful, the people die untimely. (16)
m.uttara.73.17: ‘Whatever impropriety is committed by men in towns and provinces, and if there is no protection from them, then there is indeed such untimely destruction by death. (17)
m.uttara.73.18: ‘Both in the towns and provinces it is clear that there must have been some fault in the king, there is no doubt, due to which this death of my son has occurred.’ (18)
m.uttara.73.19: Thus making such pitiful utterances again and again and keeping in check the King, inflicted by sorrow, he embraced the dead child repeatedly. (19)
m.uttara.74.1: The scion of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, heard all the pitiful lamentations of that Brāhmaṇa, full of pain and sorrow. (1)
m.uttara.74.2: Inflicted by pain He, Śrī Rāma, called His councillors, Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva and also his brothers, together with the citizens. (2)
m.uttara.74.3: Then eight Brāhmaṇas together with Vasiṣṭha were made to appear before the King comparable with the gods, and they said ‘victory to you.’ (3)
m.uttara.74.4: Mārkaṇḍeya, Maudgalya, Vāmadeva, Kaśyapa, Kātyāyana, Jābāli, Gautama and Nārada were made to enter. (4)
m.uttara.74.10: These excellent Brāhmaṇas were all provided with seats. The councillors and citizens all were suitably seated after all those effulgent ones had taken their seats. The descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, having saluted the great sages with folded hands, conveyed to them: ‘This Brāhmaṇa obstructs the royal gate. Nārada hearing those words of the King in grief, replied with these opportune words in the presence of the sages; ‘Listen, O King, how the death of child has taken place untimely. Hearing what I say, O king, descendant of Raghu, do what requires to be done. In the Kṛtayuga formerly the Brāhmaṇas alone were performers of austerities; no non-Brāhmaṇas ever practised austerities in that Yuga, inflamed by penances, and dominated by Brāhmaṇa, and also there was no prevalence of ignorance. All were born immortal ones and also possessed of distant vision; then came the Tretāyuga for men possessed of mortal frame. (5—10)
m.uttara.74.12: . ‘In Tretā, strongly built Kṣatriyas were dominant and practised austere penance. But those of Kṛtayuga were certainly superior in merit to those who belonged to Tretā (11-12)
m.uttara.74.14: ‘In Kṛtayuga Brāhmaṇas were superior and Kṣatriyas were inferior in the merits of austerity and effulgence but in Tretā both became equal and at par. (13-14)
m.uttara.74.16: ‘Tretā is dominated by Varṇāśrama Dharma. But here itself irreligion had stepped in even though on one foot, yet hereafter gradually there will be decline in Dharma. (15-16)
m.uttara.74.17: ‘The Rājasika acts like agriculture was known to be low (अनृत) and was supposed to be not recommendable. The same act in the form of a foot of irreligion was firmly rooted on the earth in Tretā. (17)
m.uttara.74.18: “This way by establishing one of his fruit in the shape of falsehood, the irreligion limited the life span of beings in Tretā in comparison to Satyayuga. (18)
m.uttara.74.19: ‘Therefore in order to save themselves from the evil effect of falsehood, one foot of irreligion, people who were dedicated to truthful conduct scrupulously practised fully auspicious deeds. (19)
m.uttara.74.21: ‘Yet in Tretā only Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas engaged themselves in observing penance. The rest of the people did servicing (like production and manual labour) out of these four categories the Vaiśyas and Śūdras got as their share—the service as their own Dharma. Śūdras particularly served and adored the other three castes. (20-21)
m.uttara.74.22: ‘O best among the kings, in the meanwhile the Tretā approaches its end, the Vaiśyas and Śūdras indulge in irreligion through falsehood as one of its feet. Then Brāhmaṇas and Kṣatriyas suffer more and more deterioration. (22)
m.uttara.74.23: ‘Then unrighteousness placed on the earth its second foot, and by that the third Yuga was counted as Dvāpara (given to two feet). (23)
m.uttara.74.24: “With the coming into existence of the Dvāparayuga, unrighteousness and Anṛta (अनृत) flourished, O bull among men. (24)
m.uttara.74.25: ‘In this Yuga, known as Dvāpara, penance entered the Vaiśya, thus through the three Yugas penance entered the three Varṇas (classes) successively. (25)
m.uttara.74.26: ‘Righteousness was established in these three Yugas resorting to the three Varṇas (classes), the Śūdra could not attain the right of penance in these Yugas, O bull among men. (26)
m.uttara.74.27: ‘O best among kings, one belonging to lower caste performs severe penances. In the future Kali age the performance of penance will go to Śūdra. (27)
m.uttara.74.28: ‘Even in Dvāpara, penance by a Śūdra is taken to be great irreligion. (Now in Tretā surely) some Śūdra is engaged in severe penance in some frontier province—the wreched one. (28)
m.uttara.74.30: ‘This infantile death is the result of the same. If some one practises Adharma in the territory of a King, it causes a great loss to the state prosperity and the king goes to hell; there is no doubt about it. (29-30)
m.uttara.74.33: ‘Righteously ruling over the subjects, the king shares one sixth portion of the merit that accrues due to pious deeds performed by study and penance, why should partaker of one sixth not protect the subjects? So you, O lion among kings, investigate your territory. Wherever you see unrighteous actions done, then make efforts to put them right; thus righteousness and long life will prevail among men, O best among men, and also the child will come back to life.’ (31—33)
m.uttara.75.1: Hearing those nectar-like words of Nārada, Śrī Rāma was highly pleased and spoke thus to Lakṣmaṇa: (1)
m.uttara.75.2: ‘O gracious one, go and console the best among Brāhmaṇas, and place the body of the dead child in an oil tub. (2)
m.uttara.75.3: ‘O gracious one, provide it (the tub) with lasting and fragrant oils, so that the body of the child may not decompose. (3)
m.uttara.75.4: ‘Make arrangements to preserve the body of the child, the innocent one, so that it may not get decomposed and the limbs are not disjointed.’ (4)
m.uttara.75.5: Having thus told the auspicious Lakṣmaṇa, the scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma summoned mentally Puṣpaka: ‘Come O famous one.’ (5)
m.uttara.75.6: Puṣpaka, adorned with gold, taking the hint came at once near the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma. (6)
m.uttara.75.7: The Puṣpaka spoke bending down, to Śrī Rāma: ‘O King of long arms, here I am, your servant, at your command.’ (7)
m.uttara.75.8: Hearing these appealing words of the Puṣpaka, the king, Śrī Rāma, having saluted the great sages, ascended the plane. (8)
m.uttara.75.10: Taking His bow and quiver and a dazzling sword, and leaving both Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata in the city, He went looking here and there to the western direction full of greenery and then proceeded to the northern direction covered by the snow-clad mountain, Himālaya. (9-10)
m.uttara.75.11: Seeing not the slightest unrighteous thing done there, then He, Śrī Rāma, scanned also the whole eastern region. (11)
m.uttara.75.13: The King, Śrī Rāma, then seated on the Puṣpaka, saw the southern quarter, where conduct was the purest, and which was as clear as the base of mirror, He saw on the northern side of the Śaivala mountain a great lake. (12-13)
m.uttara.75.14: In that lake the descendant of Raghu, the noble one, saw an ascetic performing great penances, while suspended with head turned downward. (14)
m.uttara.75.15: The son of Raghu, the kind one, Śrī Rāma, having approached that ascetic, performing great penances, said to him: ‘O performer of vows, you are great. (15)
m.uttara.75.16: ‘O powerful one, aged through penances, to which caste do you belong, I ask you out of curiosity. I am Rāma, son of King Daśaratha. (16)
m.uttara.75.17: ‘What object is desired by you to be obtained as boon, is it the attainment of the heaven or some other object, for which you perform penances, difficult to be performed by others? (17)
m.uttara.75.18: ‘For which object have you practised penances, that I want to hear, O ascetic? Are you a Brāhmaṇa? O good man, may welfare be with you, are you a Kṣatriya difficult to overcome, or belonging to the third caste, a Vaiśya, or a Śūdra? Please speak out the truth.’ (18)
m.uttara.75.19: Thus enquired by the King, the son of Daśaratha, King of Kings, that ascetic spoke of his own caste and reason for practising the penances.’ (19)
m.uttara.76.1: Hearing those words of Śrī Rāma capable of doing anything with ease, remaining with the head downwards, he (the ascetic) replied: (1)
m.uttara.76.2: ‘O famous one, I am born in the line of the Śūdra caste, and have resorted to great penance. I desire godhood, O Śrī Rāma, with this body. (2)
m.uttara.76.3: ‘I do not speak untruth as I wish to conquer the world of the gods, know me as Śūdra, Śambūka by name, O scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma.’ (3)
m.uttara.76.4: On this the descendant of Raghu, taking out dazling sword from its sheath, chopped off the head of the Śūdra, while he was speaking thus. (4)
m.uttara.76.5: On the Śūdra being killed, the gods headed by Agni together with Indra repeatedly praised the scion of the Kakutsthas saying: ‘Well done.’ (5)
m.uttara.76.6: A shower of very fragrant divine flowers, carried by the wind, fell from all sides. (6)
m.uttara.76.7: The gods highly pleased said to Śrī Rāma of true valour: ‘O king, O wise one, you have done this wonderful job for gods. (7)
m.uttara.76.8: ‘Take whatever boon you desire, O Subjugator of foes, due to your good deed this Śūdra will not attain heaven, O descendant of Raghu’. (8)
m.uttara.76.9: Hearing the words of the gods, Śrī Rāma of true valour spoke to Indra the destroyer of enemy fortresses thus: (9)
m.uttara.76.10: “If the gods are pleased, may that son of the Brāhmaṇa come back to life, grant me this boon, this is the best and most coveted boon for me. (10)
m.uttara.76.11: “The only child of the Brāhmaṇa was taken to the abode of Yama, the son of Vivasvān, untimely due to my some wrongful doing. (11)
m.uttara.76.12: “So please bring the child to life again, may welfare be with you. ‘I shall bring your child back to life,’ thus I have promised to the Brāhmaṇa. May my words not be untrue.” (12)
m.uttara.76.13: Hearing these words of Śrī Rāma, the best among the gods, highly pleased, replied to the descendant of Raghu: (13)
m.uttara.76.14: ‘Be contended, O Scion of Kakutstha, that child has come back to life and joined his kinsmen. (14)
m.uttara.76.15: ‘The moment the Śūdra was killed, that very moment this child came to life. (15)
m.uttara.76.16: ‘Hail to Thee, we wish your welfare; now we may proceed, O bull among men, O descendant of Raghu, we wish to see the hermitage of Agastya. (16)
m.uttara.76.17: ‘The brilliant one, the initiation (vow) of that Ṛṣi (sage) among Brāhmaṇas, Agastya, has come to an end, twelfth year he has passed observing the vow of sleeping on the water. (17)
m.uttara.76.18: ‘Therefore, O scion of Kakutstha, we shall go to applaud the sage, you too should go to see that great sage; we wish your welfare!’ (18)
m.uttara.76.19: ‘The descendant of the Raghus, Śrī Rāma, having promised to do so, ascended the chariot, Puṣpaka, ornamented with gold. (19)
m.uttara.76.20: Then the gods proceeded on spacious Vimānas, planes : Śrī Rāma too followed them soon to the hermitage of the pitcher-born, Agastya. (20)
m.uttara.76.21: Seeing the gods arrived, Agastya, the repository of penances, the holy one, worshipped all of them without discrimination. (21)
m.uttara.76.22: Accepting the worship and adoring the great sage, Agastya, the gods highly pleased went away to the upper-most heaven together with their followers. (22)
m.uttara.76.23: After the gods had departed, the scion of Kakutstha descending from Puṣpaka, made obeisance to the great sage, Agastya. (23)
m.uttara.76.24: Śrī Rāma paid obeisance to the noble sage, effulgent with the Tapa of austerity and having received the best hospitality, took his seat. (24)
m.uttara.76.25: Agastya, the sage of great penances, said to Śrī Rāma : ‘Welcome to you, best among men, O descendant of Raghu, it is my fortune that you have come. (25)
m.uttara.76.26: “By your excellent virtues you are worthy of adoration as my honoured guest, O king, you always dwell in my heart. (26)
m.uttara.76.27: “The gods say that You have come here after killing the Śūdra and by your righteous act, (of killing the Śūdra) You have thus restored to life the son of the Brāhmaṇa. (27)
m.uttara.76.29: “Stay one night with me, O descendant of Raghu, You are Nārāyaṇa (the abode of all souls), and all is established in You. You are lord of all the gods, the eternal Puruṣa, You may, indeed, go back to your city at dawn. (28-29)
m.uttara.76.30: “This divine ornament glowing with its own divine lusture, O gracious one, has been made by Viśvakarmā (the divine artisan). (30)
m.uttara.76.31: “Please accept this, O scion of Kakutstha, for my pleasure, a gift when offered again constitutes great merit. (31)
m.uttara.76.34: “You are worthy of wearing this ornament. You indeed are capable of giving precious gifts, and also protecting the gods together with Indra. Therefore, duly I give this to you, please accept it.” The wisest among the wise, the great charioteer of Ikṣvāku dynasty, Śrī Rāma while aware of his Kṣatriya duties, asked the Mahātmā: “Sir, accepting donation is not prohibited only for Brāhmaṇas. (32—34)
m.uttara.76.36: “O best among the Brāhmaṇas, it is strictly prohibited for the Kṣatriya to accept any charitable gift. It is more so in case a Brāhmaṇa is the donor. Kindly explain.” Having been thus enquired by Śrī Rāma, the great sage Agastya said in reply: (35-36)
m.uttara.76.37: “O Śrī Rāma! In the times during the Satyayuga, an age of Brahma, all the subjects were without a king. Later on Indra was declared as king of gods. (37)
m.uttara.76.39: Then people went to god Brahmā in order to have a king and prayed to him, ‘O Lord, you have appointed Indra as king of gods. Similarly, for us also provide a worthy man as our king, so that worshipping him we could move about in the world, becoming free of sins. (38-39)
m.uttara.76.41: ‘We shall not live without a king, This is our supreme decision.’ Then Brahmā, the highest god, after calling the guardians of regions alongwith Indra, said: ‘All of you give me a portion of your authority.’ Then all the guardians gave away a portion of their power. (40-41)
m.uttara.76.42: ‘Then Brahmā sneezed, whence was born king Kṣupa. Brahmā invested him with the entire might of the guardians (of regions given away by them). (42)
m.uttara.76.43: Then he made Kṣupa the ruling king of the people. Kṣupa after becoming king ruled the earth by virtue of the portion of the might given by Indra. (43)
m.uttara.76.51: The king nourished the people by the portion of power given to him by Varuṇa. By the portion of the mighty Kubera, he then, lent to the people the glory of Kubera, the Lord of riches. By the portion of Yama he devised punishment to the people as and when they committed sin(s). ‘O Śrī Rāma, the foremost among men! (as king, you are also invested with the might of the guardians of regions). For my deliverance accept this ornament through the portion (of the might) of Indra, O Lord ! Prosperity be unto you !’ Then Śrī Rāma accepted the divine ornament, bright like the sun, given by the high-souled hermit, and asked about his acquisition of the ornament. ‘O Eminent Brāhmaṇa ! How and from where did you acquire this divine and wonderful ornament? I am asking this out of curiosity, as you are a great repository of wonders.’ After Śrī Rāma enquired of, the sage said to Śrī Rāma, ‘Listen, O Śrī Rāma, what happened in the old Tretā age.’ (44—51)
m.uttara.77.1: “O Śrī Rāma! In the former Tretāyuga there was a forest, extending to hundred Yojanas, where there were neither animals nor birds. (1)
m.uttara.77.2: “In that forest, uninhabited by men, I practised askesis, which was the best of penances, O gracious one ! I set my foot to know all about the forest. (2)
m.uttara.77.3: “I could not indeed specify the beauty of that forest with its tasty fruits and roots and groves of various types. (3)
m.uttara.77.4: “In the midst of the forest was a lake, one Yojana wide; filled with swans and ducks and beautified with Cakrawāka birds. (4)
m.uttara.77.7: “The lake was full of lotuses and water-lilies with no trace of moss, it was a great wonder, enjoyable and excelled by none, it was clear like crystal and calm and inhabited by innumerable lovely birds. Near that lake there was a strong, brilliant, wonderful hermitage, old and extremely holy; but not inhabited by the ascetics: There O bull among men ! I dwelt one summer night. (5—7)
m.uttara.77.8: “Rising in the early morning for daybreak-duties I reached the lake and then saw there a corpse (dead body) plump and spotless shining in the water. (8)
m.uttara.77.15: Pondering over it lying with all its beauty inside the lake, I, for a moment, O descendant of Raghu, stood apart and thought: O lord, what could this be. Then all at once I saw a divine and wonderful spacious chariot yoked by swans and having the speed of mind; O scion of Raghus! I saw a denizen of the heaven on that chariot, thousands of divinely ornamented nymphs served him, some were singing, others were melodiously playing on the Mṛdaṅga (drum), lute and Paṇava (symbol), and others were dancing; Some other with lotus-like eyes fanned his face with expensive chowries with gold-handles and the lustre comparable with the rays of the moon; Then raising himself up from the throne, as the sun rises on the summits of Meru mountain, he, the denizen of heaven getting down from the chariot ate up the corpse, while I looked on, O descendant of Raghu. (9—15)
m.uttara.77.16: “Then having consumed to his satisfaction, the flesh rich in fat, the celestial being, going down the lake performed ablutions. (16)
m.uttara.77.17: “Having sipped water (in ablution) in the prescribed way that celestial being, O descendant of Raghu, got ready to ascend the excellent chariot. (17)
m.uttara.77.18: “Seeing him, who was like a god, ascending the chariot, I, on my part, spoke to him these words: ‘O bull among men ! Who are you? O god-like one, O gracious one, You should tell me why you ate this loathsome food, looked down upon by others. (18)
m.uttara.77.20: “ ‘You possess ethereal beauty. Sir, whose food could be this; therefore, O gracious one, I am wonder-struck. I wish to know the facts. I do not consider this corpse as your food in expediency.’ (19-20)
m.uttara.77.21: “Thus spoken to out of curiosity and also in well-chosen words, the celestial one, O King, having heard me, narrated all that I had enquired.” (21)
m.uttara.78.1: Hearing the words comprised of holy syllables spoken by me, O descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, the celestial being, with folded hands replied thus: (1)
m.uttara.78.2: “O Brāhmaṇa ! listen to what happened formerly, that could not be resisted and which is the cause of my pleasure and sorrow, as you desire to know it. (2)
m.uttara.78.3: “In the old days, my father Vaidarbha of great fame was possessed of great power and was known in the three worlds by the name of Sudeva. (3)
m.uttara.78.4: “Two sons were born to him from his two wives. I, the elder one, was known as Śweta, while my younger brother was known as Suratha. (4)
m.uttara.78.5: “On my father having attained heaven, the citizens consecrated me. And I ruled righteously, with care. (5)
m.uttara.78.6: “O Brāhmaṇa, observer of vows, thus a thousand years passed by, with my ruling over the kingdom and protecting my subjects. (6)
m.uttara.78.8: “ So, O best among Brāhmaṇas, knowing from some men about the span of my life, keeping in mind the approach of death, I came and entered this forest near the beautiful lake, difficult to enter and with no animals or birds residing therein to perform penances. (7-8)
m.uttara.78.9: “Having consecrated Suratha as the king, and reaching this lake, I performed penances for long. (9)
m.uttara.78.10: “Practising severe austerities for three thousand years in this great forest, I obtained the world of Brahmā (heaven) excelling all other worlds. (10)
m.uttara.78.11: “Having reached the heaven, O best among Brāhmaṇas, great hunger and thirst pained me and my senses were badly afflicted. (11)
m.uttara.78.12: “Then approaching Brahmā the best in the three worlds, I said, ‘Sir, this world of Brahmā is free from hunger and thirst. (12)
m.uttara.78.13: “ ‘As a consequence of which actions I am afflicted by hunger and thirst? What my food is, O God? O Brahmā! please tell me that’. (13)
m.uttara.78.14: “On this Brahmā told me, ‘O son of Sudeva, your food is your own tasty flesh, eat that for ever. (14)
m.uttara.78.15: “You have well-nourished your own body performing the best of penances. That which is not sown, shall never sprout O wise one. (15)
m.uttara.78.16: “You have not given even the smallest thing in charity, and have only practised great penances. Therefore, having reached heaven hunger and thirst afflict you. (16)
m.uttara.78.17: “As you eat your own body, well-nourished by edibles, full of the flavour of nectar; therefore, by that (eating flesh) you will live. (17)
m.uttara.78.18: “When the great and unconquerable sage Agastya will come to that forest, O Śweta, you will be delivered of this trouble. (18)
m.uttara.78.19: “O gracious one, Agastya is capable of delivering even the host of gods, what to say of you, afflicted with hunger and thirst, O long-armed one! (19)
m.uttara.78.20: “Thus having learnt of the decision of the god of the gods, Brahmā, O best among men, I make food of my own body. (20)
m.uttara.78.21: “O Brāhmaṇa, this body does not exhaust, although enjoyed by me for many years, and O Ṛṣi! I am fully quenched too. (21)
m.uttara.78.22: “So deliver me—troubled one, from the difficulty. None other than Agastya, the pitcher-born ascetic, has power to do so. (22)
m.uttara.78.23: “O gracious one, best among Brāhmaṇas, accept this ornament for wearing, may welfare be with you. Please favour me by accepting this. (23)
m.uttara.78.24: “All this gold, wealth, apparel, edibles and enjoyables, O Ṛṣi among Brāhmaṇas, I offer you as also the ornaments. (24)
m.uttara.78.25: “All desirables and enjoyables also I surrender to you. I deserve to be favoured by you by releasing me of troubles.” (25)
m.uttara.78.26: ‘Having heard these words full of sorrow from the celestial one, I accepted this wonderful ornament for releaving him. (26)
m.uttara.78.28: ‘As soon as I accepted that auspicious ornament, the former body of the Ṛṣi among kings (Śweta) vanished and the Ṛṣi among kings, extremely happy and satisfied, went to the heaven. (27-28)
m.uttara.78.29: ‘By him (Śweta) equal to Indra, this divine ornament, of wonderful form, was given to me, O scion of Kakutstha, for that purpose.’ (29)
m.uttara.79.1: Hearing that most wonderful and marvellous story, narrated by Agastya, Śrī Rāma asked him again, full of dismay and reverence. (1)
m.uttara.79.2: “Sir, how was that fearful forest, where the Vaidarbhaka king Śweta was performing penances, devoid of animals and birds. (2)
m.uttara.79.3: “I wish to know in detail how that king entered that forest, which was barren and uninhabited by men, to perform penances.” (3)
m.uttara.79.4: Hearing the words of Śrī Rāma uttered out of curiosity, the highly powerful one, Agastya, spoke thus: (4)
m.uttara.79.5: “In the former Kṛtayuga, Manu (Vaivasvata) was the king. His son, a joy to his family, was the famous Ikṣvāku. (5)
m.uttara.79.6: “Placing the first son, Ikṣvāku, unconquerable on the earth, incharge of the kingdom, Manu said to him: ‘Be the progenitor of all royal families.’ (6)
m.uttara.79.7: “Then, O descendant of Raghu, the son promised to do so and being fully satisfied Manu addressed him thus. (7)
m.uttara.79.8: “O noble one, I am pleased, you will be the forerunner of all royal families, there is no doubt. By punishment as a sign of authority protect the subjects; do not mete out unnecessary punishments. (8)
m.uttara.79.9: “That form of punishment, which is meted out to the guilty men, being given in proper manner, leads the king to heaven. (9)
m.uttara.79.10: “Therefore, O dear son of long arms, make efforts to mete out punishment according to prescriptions in the Śāstras. Resorting to just punishment properly, you will attain great righteousness.” (10)
