m.uttara.79.11: Thus, having instructed him, Manu, pleased with himself, went to the eternal abode of Brahmā through Samādhi (trance). (11)
m.uttara.79.12: When Manu had left for heaven, Ikṣvāku of unlimited brilliance, fell to thinking, ‘How shall I produce sons?’ (12)
m.uttara.79.13: Through true actions of many types, then the son of Manu, the pious one, procreated the hundred sons, comparable with the sons of the gods. (13)
m.uttara.79.15: The youngest one of them, was ignorant, and illiterate and did not serve his elders. His father gave him, dull-witted son, the name ‘Daṇḍa’, thinking that physical punishment shall certainly be the fate of this one (son). (14-15)
m.uttara.79.16: “Not seeing any territory fully fearful, the father gave him the kingdom situated between the Vindhya and Śaivala mountains. (16)
m.uttara.79.17: “That Daṇḍa became the king of that territory situated at the foot of the mountains and established a city unmatched and the best (among the cities). (17)
m.uttara.79.18: “Daṇḍa named the city Madhumanta, O lord, and chose as his chief priest Uśanā, rich in vows. (18)
m.uttara.79.19: “Thus that king, Daṇḍa, ruled over that kingdom together with the chief priest, the Kingdom being filled with joyful men as the king of gods rules in the heaven. (19)
m.uttara.79.20: “Then that King, Daṇḍa, the grandson of Manu, together with Uśana of great fame, ruled as a highly pious king, like Indra ruling over the gods.” (20)
m.uttara.80.1: Having thus narrated the story of Ikṣvāku to Śrī Rāma, the great sage, Agastya, the pitcher-born one, began to narrate another story connected with the same. (1)
m.uttara.80.2: ‘Then, O scion of Kakutstha, that Daṇḍa, the self-controlled one, ruled over that kingdom there, uprooting all foes, for successively ten thousand years. (2)
m.uttara.80.3: Then at one time the king, Daṇḍa, went to the beautiful hermitage of sage Bhārgava (Śukra), in the enjoyable month of Caitra. (3)
m.uttara.80.4: There Daṇḍa saw the daughter of Bhārgava, a paragon of beauty, roaming about in the forest. (4)
m.uttara.80.5: Having seen her, that wicked minded Daṇḍa, dull-witted, one afflicted by the arrows of cupid, greatly agitated approached the daughter of Bhārgava and said: (5)
m.uttara.80.6: ‘O one of beautiful hips and loins, wherefrom do you hail, O beautiful one ! whose daughter you are? O of auspicious face, afflicted as I am by cupid, I ask you.’ (6)
m.uttara.80.7: When he said so, blinded by the sexual urge and madly infatuated as he was, the daughter of Bhārgava replied thus courteously: (7)
m.uttara.80.8: ‘Know me as the daughter of the lord Bhārgava, unwearied in action, named Arajā, the eldest one residing in the hermitage. (8)
m.uttara.80.9: ‘Do not touch me by force, I am under the control of my father, O best among kings. My father is your preceptor and you are the pupil of that noble one. (9)
m.uttara.80.11: ‘Enraged, he (Bhārgava), the performer of great penances, shall cause you much grief. If, however, for something other than mere passion, you desire me, then ask my hand following the righteous path from my father, O best among men; otherwise you will meet with frightful consequences. (10-11)
m.uttara.80.12: ‘In anger my father would burn up the three worlds O one of perfect limbs. He will give me to you if asked for.’ (12)
m.uttara.80.13: To Arajā speaking thus, Daṇḍa under the power of cupid, intoxicated with passion, replied folding his hands over his head: (13)
m.uttara.80.14: ‘Please favour me, O one of beautiful hips and loins, do not delay, O beautiful one, my vital breaths are shattering on your account. (14)
m.uttara.80.15: ‘By possessing you, let there be my death, or a great sin committed, accept me, devoted to you and asking for you, highly agitated.’ (15)
m.uttara.80.16: Thus saying, he, Daṇḍa, the strong one, seizing the trembling daughter of Bhārgava between his arms by force, he raped her. (16)
m.uttara.80.17: Having committed that terrible heinous crime, he went back soon to the unparalleled Madhumanta. (17)
m.uttara.80.18: That Arajā too, remained weeping near the hermitage, and in great fright waited for her father, who was just like a god. (18)
m.uttara.81.1: Having heard the account of Arajā that gracious divine Ṛṣi Bhārgava came back at once to his hermitage surrounded by his pupils, although bitten by hunger. (1)
m.uttara.81.2: He saw the pitiable Arajā covered with semen, as the full-moon at dawn faded out due to being eclipsed. (2)
m.uttara.81.3: Anger flared up in him, specially as he was bitten by hunger, as if to burn the three worlds, and he said to his pupils: (3)
m.uttara.81.4: “See how this performer of action contrary to good conduct, and ignorant one meets with severe calamities produced by me in anger, and comparable with the flames of fire. (4)
m.uttara.81.5: “Destruction is the fate of that dull-witted one who wishes to touch the flames of the kindled fire. (5)
m.uttara.81.6: “As he has committed this heinous crime, so this dull-witted one will get the fruit of his sin. (6)
m.uttara.81.7: “In seven nights, this king, the dull-witted one, with his sons, army and carriers, and of sinful conduct, shall meet with death. (7)
m.uttara.81.8: “For a hundred Yojanas all round, the territory of this dull-witted one, the extirpator of Pāka, Indra shall burn up with a shower of dust. (8)
m.uttara.81.9: “All beings, stationary and moving, that are here, will perish due to this heavy shower of dust. (9)
m.uttara.81.10: “After seven nights, the prosperous territory of Daṇḍa will entirely disappear alongwith the shower of dust.” (10)
m.uttara.81.11: Thus speaking to the inhabitors of the hermitage, he, Bhārgava, possessed of red eyes with rage said to them again, ‘stay at the outskirts of this territory.’ (11)
m.uttara.81.12: Hearing these words of Uśanā, the Āśrama-dwellers, went out of his territory and made place for themselves elsewhere. (12)
m.uttara.81.13: Having thus spoken to the ascetics, Bhārgava then addressed Arajā, “O dull-witted, you will stay in this Āśrama, conscious of your duties. (13)
m.uttara.81.14: “O Arajā, free from worry, enjoy this lake of beautiful form and extending to a Yojana, and also wait for some time. (14)
m.uttara.81.15: “Those beings, who will come to stay near you for a night, will be unassailable forever by the shower of dust.” (15)
m.uttara.81.16: “On hearing the command of the Brahmarṣi, Arajā, the daughter of Bhṛgu, despite being very much pained said to her father “Very well.” (16)
m.uttara.81.19: “Having said this, Bhṛgu took up his abode elsewhere. That kingdom of the chief of the kings alongwith his servants, the army and the vehicles, was reduced to ashes within seven days, as was declared by the Brahmavādī Bhṛgu. This kingdom of Daṇḍa lying between the Vindhya and the Śaivala mountains, was cursed by the Brahmarṣi, since Daṇḍa had acted unrighteously. Since then, O descendant of Kakutstha, it has been called Daṇḍakāraṇya. (17—19)
m.uttara.81.20: “Since ascetics came and inhabited here it has been known as ‘Janasthāna’, O Rāma ! I have told you everything about what you enquired of me. (20)
m.uttara.81.22: “O Valiant one ! The time for the performance of Sandhyā is passing. All these great sages, O foremost among men ! after having finished their bath, are worshipping the sun, with their respective pitcher filled with water. The sun, having accepted the worship in the form of recitation of Vedic hymns by the knowers of Brahma, has set in. You also go and take bath and sip water and perform Sandhyā.” (21-22)
m.uttara.82.1: Having heard with reverence the words of the sage, Agastya, Śrī Rāma approached the holy lake inhabited by the host of Apsarās, for performing his evening adoration. (1)
m.uttara.82.2: Having sipped the water there and performed the evening Pūjā, Śrī Rāma entered the hermitage of Agastya, the holy pitcher-born one. (2)
m.uttara.82.3: Agastya offered to him for food radish of good quality and also purified rice and other edibles. (3)
m.uttara.82.4: That best among men, Śrī Rāma, enjoyed that food comparable with nectar, was highly pleased and satisfied. He spent that night together with the sage. (4)
m.uttara.82.5: Śrī Rāma, the best among the Raghus, the tamer of foes, getting up at dawn and having performed the morning daily rites, approached the sage to beg leave of him and to depart. (5)
m.uttara.82.6: Having saluted the great sage, born of the pitcher, Agastya, Śrī Rāma said to him: ‘I beg leave of you to depart to my own capital; may you permit me to do so. (6)
m.uttara.82.7: ‘I am fortunate having been favoured by seeing you. I shall come again to see you, O holy one, for purification of myself.’ (7)
m.uttara.82.8: While Rāma spoke in this marvellous manner, the great ascetic possessed of virtuous vision was highly pleased and said : (8)
m.uttara.82.9: ‘O Rāma, your speech of auspicious syllables is indeed wonderful, O descendant of Raghu, you are the purifier of all beings. (9)
m.uttara.82.10: ‘The few who see you even for a moment, are purified, and attain heaven, and are worshipped by the lord of heaven (gods). (10)
m.uttara.82.11: “Those beings on earth, who see you with inimical eyes, they are instantly struck by the rod of Yama and descend to hell. (11)
m.uttara.82.12: ‘O best among the Raghus, in this manner you are the purifier of all mortals, O scion of Raghu. The one describing Your sports (Līlās) on earth shall attain perfection. (12)
m.uttara.82.13: ‘You go with pleasure on your path unagitated and without fear and rule over your Kingdom righteously; you are the resort of this world.’ (13)
m.uttara.82.14: Thus spoken to by the sage, the king with folded and outstretched hands, the wise one, saluted that sage of truthful conduct. (14)
m.uttara.82.15: Saluting the best among sages, Agastya, and all other great ascetics, he ascended unagitated that Puṣpaka, ornamented with gold. (15)
m.uttara.82.16: The host of sages on all sides honoured him with blessings as the gods honour Indra, the thousand-eyed one. (16)
m.uttara.82.17: The well-composed Śrī Rāma on the Puṣpaka, ornamented with gold, looked like the moon near the cloud at the approach of the rainy season. (17)
m.uttara.82.18: Then, by the advent of midday, being honoured here and there, and having reached Ayodhyā, the scion of Kakutstha descended in the middle of the city. (18)
m.uttara.82.19: Then leaving the beautiful Puṣpaka, moving at will, He said: ‘Leaving me, go to Kubera, O powerful one; may welfare be with thee.’ (19)
m.uttara.82.20: Then Śrī Rāma hurriedly ordered the door-keeper in the other apartment : ‘Go to Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, those two of swift valour, and having conveyed to them my arrival, call them here, do not delay.’ (20)
m.uttara.83.1: Having heard the words of Śrī Rāma, who was unwearied in performance, the door-keeper called the two princes and they reported to the scion of Raghu. (1)
m.uttara.83.2: The scion of the Raghus seeing both the princes arrived, embraced them and then spoke to them these words : (2)
m.uttara.83.3: “I have done the service to the Brāhmaṇa as expected. Now I want to perform Rājasūya—the outer limit of piety, O brothers. (3)
m.uttara.83.4: “In my opinion the bridge of righteousness is imperishable and unchangeable; the discourse on righteousness destroys all sins. (4)
m.uttara.83.5: “Together with both of you, who are dear to me as myself, I wish to perform the excellent Rājasūya. Therein resides eternal righteousness. (5)
m.uttara.83.6: “The killer of foes, Mitra, attained the position of Varuṇa, having performed the Rājasūya with proper offerings and sacrifice. (6)
m.uttara.83.7: “The knower of Dharma (Law), Soma, having performed the Rājasūya, righteously, attained fame and eternal place in all the worlds. (7)
m.uttara.83.8: “Reflect on what is the best this day together with me, you two active ones should tell me what is good for the world and also what is proper for the future.” (8)
m.uttara.83.9: Hearing these words of the scion of Raghus, Śrī Rāma, Bharata, proficient in speaking, spoke thus, folding his hands: (9)
m.uttara.83.10: “O righteous one, in you is established the highest form of righteousness, this entire earth and all fame, O one of long arms and possessing uncomparable valour. (10)
m.uttara.83.11: “All kings like us, look upon Thee, O holy one, the lord of worlds as the gods look upon Prajāpati. (11)
m.uttara.83.12: “O King, O Raghunandana of mighty strength, all kings regard you as sons look to their fathers. You are the resort of this world and also of all beings, O scion of Raghu. (12)
m.uttara.83.13: “How, O king, you being so, wish to perform the Rājasūya sacrifice, in which there shall be the destruction of royal families on earth. (13)
m.uttara.83.14: “O King, those men, who on this earth are possessed of valour, all of them will be destroyed in that Yajña due to the anger of all. (14)
m.uttara.83.15: “O lion among men, possessed of unparalleled valour, accompanied with merits, it befits you not to destroy this earth, all indeed are under your sway.” (15)
m.uttara.83.17: Hearing these nectar-like words of Bharata, Śrī Rāma of true valour was extremely pleased and said these auspicious words to the enhancer of the joy of Kaikeyī, Bharata: ‘I am pleased and satisfied today at what you say, O sinless one. (16-17)
m.uttara.83.18: ‘These words spoken by you are potent and accompanied by righteousness. O tiger among men, as they relate to the protection of the earth. (18)
m.uttara.83.19: ‘I refrain, after what you have said, from the performance of the excellent sacrifice, Rājasūya, that was our intention, O Knower of Dharma (Law). (19)
m.uttara.83.20: ‘That action is not to be undertaken by the wise which causes pain to the worlds, O elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa. The words even of the young ones are worthy of acceptance if they are carrier of good. Therefore, I have listened to your sagacious talk, O mighty one; you have spoken so well.’ (20)
m.uttara.84.1: When Śrī Rāma and the noble Bharata had spoken thus, Lakṣmaṇa addressed these auspicious words to Śrī Rāma: (1)
m.uttara.84.2: “O descendant of Raghu, the great sacrifice, Aśvamedha, is the purifier of all sins and shall be your purifier, although difficult to perform, if you so please. (2)
m.uttara.84.3: “The legend about the very noble Vāsava (Indra) is heard, that Indra tainted by the sin of the killing of Brāhmaṇa was purified by the Horse-sacrifice. (3)
m.uttara.84.4: “In the ancient times, O one of long arms, in the struggle that ensued between the gods and demons, there happened to be the mighty Vṛtra, son of Diti, honoured by the worlds. (4)
m.uttara.84.5: “A hundred Yojanas horizontally and thrice in height, he out of affection for three worlds, looked on all beings with compassion. (5)
m.uttara.84.6: “Righteous and dutiful and well-composed in mind, he ruled over this wide earth righteously with great care. (6)
m.uttara.84.7: “In his reign the earth yielded all such desirable and flavoured things, as flowers, roots and fruits. (7)
m.uttara.84.8: “The earth belonging to him yielded forth fruits without being ploughed. He ruled over that sort of kingdom, prosperous with wonderful appearance. (8)
m.uttara.84.9: “It arose in his mind: ‘I shall perform the penance unequalled, penance is indeed the highest form of welfare; all other forms of happiness are out of illusions.’ (9)
m.uttara.84.10: “Leaving his eldest son, Madhureśwara, as in-charge of the citizens, he performed frightful penances, tormenting all gods. (10)
m.uttara.84.11: “On Vṛtra performing penances, Vāsava (Indra) being highly afraid, approaching Viṣṇu spoke thus, indeed. (11)
m.uttara.84.12: “ ‘O one of long arms, all the worlds have been conquered by him performing penances, he is righteous and powerful, I cannot subdue him. (12)
m.uttara.84.13: “ ‘If again he performs penances, all beings of the worlds will be under him. (13)
m.uttara.84.14: “ ‘O powerful one, you are overlooking this demon, O lord of the gods, if you are in anger, Vṛtra will not stand even for a moment. (14)
m.uttara.84.15: “ ‘Ever since you patronised him, he has attained supremacy over the worlds. (15)
m.uttara.84.16: “So, have mercy on the worlds now; by your favour, indeed, this world will be free from pain. (16)
m.uttara.84.17: “These denizens of heaven (gods) look upon Thee, O Viṣṇu, please help them by killing the mighty Vṛtra. (17)
m.uttara.84.18: “By you forever succour was given to the noble ones i.e., gods. For others these ignoble Asuras are unbearable. You, Sir, are the resort of those who have no shelter.” (18)
m.uttara.85.1: Hearing those words of Lakṣmaṇa, the extirpator of foes, Śrī Rāma, said: ‘O observer of vows, narrate in totality the killing of Vṛtra.’ (1)
m.uttara.85.2: Being thus spoken to by the scion of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, the enhancer of the joy of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, the observer of vows, narrated the divine story of the killing of Vṛtra again. (2)
m.uttara.85.3: ‘Having heard the words of the thousand-eyed one, Indra, and also of all the gods, Viṣṇu spoke thus to all the gods headed by Indra. (3)
m.uttara.85.4: ‘Formerly I was attached affectionately to Vṛtra here and thus for your good indeed I am not killing the great Asura. (4)
m.uttara.85.5: ‘That which leads to your great happiness, has indeed to be performed: Therefore, I shall tell you the means by which Vṛtra will be killed; the thousand-eyed one, Indra, will kill Vṛtra. (5)
m.uttara.85.6: ‘O best among gods, I shall divide myself threefold, by that the thousand-eyed one, Indra, will indeed kill Vṛtra. There is no doubt about it. (6)
m.uttara.85.7: ‘One part of mine may go to Vāsava (Indra), the second part may enter the thunderbolt and third, the earth; then Indra shall kill Vṛtra.’ (7)
m.uttara.85.8: On the lord of gods, Viṣṇu, speaking thus, the gods then said: ‘This is as You say, there is no doubt, O killer of the Daityas, sons of Diti. (8)
m.uttara.85.9: ‘Let welfare be with You, we shall now depart desiring the killing of the Asura, Vṛtra. O extremely liberal one, Viṣṇu, may you bestow Vāsava with your power.’ (9)
m.uttara.85.10: Then all the noble ones headed by the thousand-eyed god, Indra, went to that forest where the great Asura, Vṛtra, was. (10)
m.uttara.85.11: They saw the mighty Asura possessed of his own power performing penance, as if drinking the three worlds and burning up the sky. (11)
m.uttara.85.12: On seeing the best of Asuras, gods were frightened, and thought ‘how shall we kill him, and how indeed we shall not be conquered by him?’ (12)
m.uttara.85.13: While the gods were thus contemplating, the thousand-eyed one, the destroyer of fortress, Indra, taking hold of the thunderbolt with both of his hands, hurled it at the head of Vṛtra. (13)
m.uttara.85.14: When the head of Vṛtra struck by the thunderbolt, blazing like fire of destruction and inflamed by its own lustre, fell down, it simultaneously terrified the whole universe. (14)
m.uttara.85.15: The lord of the gods, possessed of fame, Indra, thinking that the killing of Vṛtra was not proper, fled soon to the ends of the earth out of fear. (15)
m.uttara.85.16: The slaughter of a Brāhmaṇa pursued Indra, fleeing fast and pervaded his limbs; sorrow came upon Indra. (16)
m.uttara.85.17: With their foe killed, and bereft of Indra, the gods, with Agni at their head, worshipped Viṣṇu, the lord of the three worlds again and again. (17)
m.uttara.85.18: ‘O mightiest of all, you are the resort, and being born first, the father of this earth, you assumed the form of Viṣṇu for the protection of all beings. (18)
m.uttara.85.19: ‘By you Vṛtra is killed; the slaughter of a Brāhmaṇa afflicts Vāsava (Indra), O lion among gods. Kindly arrange for his deliverance.’ (19)
m.uttara.85.20: Hearing those words of the gods, Viṣṇu said “Let Indra worship me, I shall purify the carrier of the thunderbolt. (20)
m.uttara.85.21: “Having propitiated me through the holy Aśvamedha, the humbler of Pāka, Indra, shall again attain the position of Indra among the gods, without fear from anywhere.” (21)
m.uttara.85.22: Thus pronouncing those nectar-like words before the gods, the lord of the gods, Viṣṇu, being eulogized by the gods, proceeded to heaven. (22)
m.uttara.86.2: That Lakṣmaṇa, having narrated the whole episode of the slaying of Vṛtra, proceeded to describe the remaining part of the story. On, Vṛtra of mighty power, a terror to the gods, being killed, Indra, the killer of Vṛtra, afflicted by the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, became unconscious. (1-2)
m.uttara.86.3: Deprived of consciousness, he (Indra) went beyond the border of the world, where he remained for sometime as if writhing like a snake. (3)
m.uttara.86.5: The thousand-eyed one, Indra, having disappeared, the world was agitated, and the earth lost its form, moisture and the forestations, all lakes and rivulets dried up, commotion prevailed among beings due to draught. (4-5)
m.uttara.86.6: When the world was tottering, the gods agitated in mind, started the sacrifice that had been mentioned by Viṣṇu formerly. (6)
m.uttara.86.7: Then all hosts of gods, together with the preceptors and the sages, approached the place where Indra was hiding, quite unconscious due to fear. (7)
m.uttara.86.8: Having seen the thousand-eyed one possessed by the sin of Brāhmaṇa-slaughter, the gods performed the Aśvamedha with their Lord, Indra, at their head. (8)
m.uttara.86.9: Then, O lord of men, Śrī Rāma, the mighty Aśvamedha yajña came to be performed for the purification of the noble Mahendra (Indra) from the Brahma-hatyā. (9)
m.uttara.86.10: Then as the sacrifice, Aśvamedha, came to an end, Brahma hatyā (in person) of the noble Indra approached the gods and said : ‘Where would you give me place?’ (10)
m.uttara.86.11: Then the gods satisfied, happily said to her (the Brahma-hatyā), ‘O one difficult to reach, divide yourself four-fold.’ (11)
m.uttara.86.12: Having heard the words of the noble gods, Brahma-hatyā (in person) split itself, and staying with difficulty in Indra’s person, chose shelter elsewhere. (12)
m.uttara.86.13: ‘By one part, I shall stay for four months of the rainy season, shattering the pride of sinful ones and moving at will in the rivers swollen with water. (13)
m.uttara.86.14: By another part, I shall stay for all times on earth, there is no doubt, I speak out the truth to you all. (14)
m.uttara.86.15: By the part which is my third one, I shall stay for three nights every month in the proud and youthful women, destroying their pride. (15)
m.uttara.86.16: Those who kill innocent Brāhmaṇas on false pleas, them I shall attack by the fourth part, O bulls among gods.’ (16)
m.uttara.86.17: Then the gods replied : ‘O one of painful stay, may all that be as you say, do as you like.’ (17)
m.uttara.86.18: Then the gods fully pleased saluted the thousand-eyed one, Vāsava (Indra), since he was now carefree and purified from sin. (18)
m.uttara.86.19: On Indra being established again, the whole world was rendered calm, then Indra worshipped through the wonderful sacrifice, Aśvamedha. (19)
m.uttara.86.20: O descendant of Raghu, this is the results from Aśvamedha. So, O fortunate one, O King, perform the Aśvamedha sacrifice. (20)
m.uttara.86.21: Having heard the beautiful and charming words of Lakṣmaṇa, the king Śrī Rāmacandra, a great soul and equal to Indra in might and valour, was very much pleased and fully satisfied. (21)
m.uttara.87.1: Having heard the words spoken by Lakṣmaṇa, the mighty scion of Raghu, knower of the import of words, replied smilingly to him: (1)
m.uttara.87.2: “O best among men, Lakṣmaṇa, it is as you say, all that you say about the killing of Vṛtra and also the fruit of the horse-sacrifice. (2)
m.uttara.87.3: “O gracious one, it is heard that in the former days there was prosperous and pious Ila, ruler of Bāhlīka and the son of the Prajāpati Kardama. (3)
m.uttara.87.4: “That King of high fame, having brought under his sway the whole earth, protected the kingdom like his son O tiger among men, Lakṣmaṇa. (4)
m.uttara.87.6: “He was honoured always, O gracious one, by the liberal gods and the wealthy sons of Diti, and also by the Nāgas, Rākṣasas, Gandharvas and even the noble Yakṣas, possessed of fear. The three worlds were frightened when the powerful one was in rage. (5-6)
m.uttara.87.7: “That king, lord of Bāhlīka, of high fame, although so proficient in righteousness and valour, was very liberal at heart. (7)
m.uttara.87.8: “That one of long arms went out to hunt in a beautiful forest together with his attendants, army and carriers in the charming month of Caitra. (8)
m.uttara.87.9: “The King killed hundreds and thousands of animals in the forest. Having killed them, however, the noble king was not satisfied. (9)
m.uttara.87.10: “By that noble one were killed ten thousand animals of many species, he reached the place, where Mahāsena (Kārtikeya) was born. (10)
m.uttara.87.11: In that place the Lord of gods, the unconquerable Hara (Śiva), living with His attendants dallied with the daughter of the lord of mountains, Pārvatī. (11)
m.uttara.87.12: Assuming himself the form of a woman, desiring to please the Devī Pārvatī, the lord, having the bull as emblem, stayed near that hilly stream: (12)
m.uttara.87.13: Whatever masculine beings were there in the forest, all of them and even the trees’ masculine names were changed in the form of female beings. (13)
m.uttara.87.16: Whatever there was, was rendered feminine. In the meantime that King Ila, the son of Kardama, killing thousands of animals reached that place, and seeing all reptiles, animals and birds rendered feminine, and also himself together with his followers turned into feminine, he felt great sorrow, specially seeing himself in that form. (14—16)
m.uttara.87.20: Knowing that it was wrought by the lord of Umā, Śiva, he was afraid. Then the King together with the army and carriers sought refuge in the mighty lord, the blue-throated and skull-adorned one; the great lord Śiva, giver of boons, together with goddess Pārvatī, himself spoke to the son of Prajāpati: ‘Arise, O Ṛṣi among Kings, O mighty one, son of Kardama, performer of vows, gracious one, barring manhood ask for any boon’. Then that King being thus rebuffed, was afflicted by sorrow. (17—20)
m.uttara.87.24: Having become a woman, he did not ask for any other boon from the Lord of the gods, Śiva. Then in great sorrow, the King paying obeisance to the daughter of the lord of mountains, Pārvatī, with all his heart, said: ‘O goddess of boons, giver of boons, you are the loveliest woman of the worlds. O goddess whose vision is fruitful, with your benevolent eye favour me. Knowing what was in the mind of the Ṛṣi among kings, Ila, She spoke these auspicious words approved by Lord Śiva in his presence: ‘The giver of one half of the boon is the Lord and that of the other half I am the giver. (21—24)
m.uttara.87.29: ‘Therefore, accept half of the period as a woman and the other half as man for as long as you desire.’ Hearing this most wonderful and excellent boon being granted by the goddess, highly pleased the king then said: ‘O goddess, possessed of loveliness, uncomparable on this earth, if thou art pleased with me, I may remain as man for a month, and a woman for the other,’ The goddess of lovely face, having known the desire of the king, replied in these auspicious words : ‘Thus will it be; O king, becoming a man you shall not remember your woman-hood. Becoming a woman too you shall not remember your manhood’. Thus that King, son of Kardama, became a man for one month and a most beautiful lady in the next, i.e., one month Ila and one month Ilā). (25—29)
m.uttara.88.1: Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata were extremely wonderstruck, after hearing the story of Ila, narrated by Śrī Rāma. (1)
m.uttara.88.2: Both of them again asked Śrī Rāma with folded hands to delineate in detail the story of Ila and also his double form: (2)
m.uttara.88.3: ‘Being formed into a woman, how did the king fare in misery, and when he was changed into a male, what was his way of life.’ (3)
m.uttara.88.4: Hearing the words of the two, spoken out of curiosity, Śrī Rāma, the scion of Kakutstha narrated the story of that king as was traditionally handed down: (4)
m.uttara.88.5: ‘Becoming a lady matchlessly beautiful for the first month, (he) was surrounded by those (women), who formerly followed him in their masculine form. (5)
m.uttara.88.6: ‘The feminine bea She the unparalleled beauty of the worlds having penetrated that forest full of trees, chesters and creepers, roamed on foot, possessed of eyes like lotus-petals. (6)
m.uttara.88.7: ‘Leaving aside all carriers, Ilā then sported on in that cavity of the great mountain. (7)
m.uttara.88.8: ‘Then in that forest, not far from the mountain, was a pond beautiful in appearance, abided by many groups of birds. (8)
m.uttara.88.10: ‘Ilā then saw in that lake Budha, the son of Soma (moon), quite youthful, effulgent with his own brilliant form as if (he was) the moon arisen. He was performing severe penance inside the waters of the lake, producing fame and fulfilling desires. (9-10)
m.uttara.88.11: ‘O descendant of Raghu, fully amazed, she stirred up the entire lake together with those former men changed into women. (11)
m.uttara.88.12: ‘Budha on seeing her, came under the influence of the arrow of cupid, he could not control himself and moved in the waters. (12)
m.uttara.88.13: ‘Perceiving Ilā, who was more auspicious than any other in the three worlds, it came to his mind: ‘Who indeed is She, lovlier than a goddess. (13)
m.uttara.88.14: ‘I have not seen formerly any woman possessed of such beauty among the goddesses, the female Nāgas, the wives of Asuras or even the Apsarās. (14)
m.uttara.88.15: “If not wedded to another, she may be favourable to me. Thus thinking, Budha came out of the waters on the bank of the lake. (15)
m.uttara.88.16: ‘Reaching the hermitage, he, the noble one, called those beautiful women, and they all also saluted him. (16)
m.uttara.88.17: ‘He, the noble one, then enquired of those women, thus : ‘To whom belongs this faminine beauty of the worlds? Why has she come, please let me know fully without delay?’ (17)
m.uttara.88.18: Hearing those words of his, spoken with sweet syllables, all those women replied in sweet tones: (18)
m.uttara.88.19: ‘This woman of beautiful limbs always commands us, is unmarried and roams about in the forest alongwith us.’ (19)
m.uttara.88.20: ‘Having heard the words of unmanifest syllables of those women, that Brāhmaṇa (Budha) recited the holy Āvartanī Vidyā Stotra or chantings. (20)
m.uttara.88.21: Having thus known the whole account of that king, as it had happened, the great ascetic then spoke to all those women: (21)
m.uttara.88.22: ‘Beside at the foot of this mountain as Kiṁpuruṣīs, find out your residence soon of this mountain. (22)
m.uttara.88.23: ‘Subsist always on roots, leaves and fruits all of you women, and obtain Kiṁpuruṣas as husbands.’ (23)
m.uttara.88.24: Then those women hearing the words of the son of Soma, changed into Kiṁpuruṣīs, resided near the mountain in a large number. (24)
m.uttara.89.1: Having heard the account of the origin of Kiṁpuruṣas, Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata said to Śrī Rāma the king: ‘O Lord, how wonderful it is!’ (1)
m.uttara.89.2: Then Śrī Rāma, the noble one, continued to narrate the story of Ila, the son of Prajāpati: (2)
m.uttara.89.3: ‘Seeing that all the female Kinnaras (Kiṁpuruṣas) had departed, the great sage, Budha, said to that beautiful woman, Ilā, as if laughing: (3)
m.uttara.89.4: ‘O one of beautiful face, I am the beloved son of Soma, the moon-god; kindly look at me with love and own me.’ (4)
m.uttara.89.5: ‘Having heard those words of Budha, Ilā, left by her friends, alone, spoke to the beautiful and lustrous one, Budha: (5)
m.uttara.89.6: ‘O son of Soma, although free to move at will, I am now at your command, order me and do as you like.’ (6)
m.uttara.89.7: Hearing these wonderful words of her, Ilā, that lover, Budha, the son of the moon, was highly pleased and dallied with her. (7)
m.uttara.89.8: While Budha was dallying with Ilā of beautiful face, the spring season passed away just like a moment. (8)
m.uttara.89.9: After the lapse of a month, Ila the prosperous son of Prajāpati, having a face comparable to the full moon, woke up in bed. (9)
m.uttara.89.10: He saw that son of Soma was performing penance in that lake, with his hand raised upwards and without any support and addressed him thus: (10)
m.uttara.89.11: ‘Sir, I entered the impenetrable forest with my attendants for hunting; I do not, however, see my army, where they have gone, they who belonged to me.’ (11)
m.uttara.89.12: Having heard those words of the bull among Kings, who had lost his consciousness formerly, he, Budha, replied to him in very auspicious words, consoling him: (12)
m.uttara.89.13: ‘Your servants were killed by a hail storm; you, however, filled with fear of wind and rain fell asleep in the hermitage. (13)
m.uttara.89.14: ‘Do not feel fear or worry. Be consoled and well. O brave one, live here happily, consuming fruits and roots.’ (14)
m.uttara.89.15: The King possessed of wisdom having regained confidence by those words, replied auspiciously, feeling grieved on the perishing of his attendants. (15)
m.uttara.89.16: ‘I shall forsake my kingdom, having lost my attendants; I shall not subsist even for a moment, O Brāhmaṇa, you should advise me : what to do. (16)
m.uttara.89.17: ‘My righteous and famous son, O best among Brāhmaṇas, is well-known by the name of Śaśabindu. He shall possess my kingdom. (17)
m.uttara.89.18: ‘Having lost my attendants and spouses, who were happy, O powerful one, I shall not be able to say anything inauspicious.’ (18)
m.uttara.89.19: When the king said so, Budha said in a very pleasing manner consoling him, ‘O king, you may stay here in the Āśrama happily.’ (19)
m.uttara.89.20: ‘O mighty one, son of Kardama, you should not be grieved. I shall do well to you, after you have passed a year here.’ (20)
m.uttara.89.21: Hearing those amiable words of that Budha, unwearied in performance, the king contemplated, residing there as advised by the discourses on Brahma by Budha. (21)
m.uttara.89.22: Then he, there becoming a woman, dallied constantly for ever for a month; and as a man he contemplated righteous performance for a month. (22)
m.uttara.89.23: Then that Ilā begot a powerful son, Purūravā in the ninth month, by Budha, the son of Soma. (23)
m.uttara.89.24: That one of beautiful loins, Ilā, handed over her son possessed of great power, and similar to his father, Budha, in appearance, to his father as he was born. (24)
m.uttara.89.25: For the remaining months in the completion of a year, Budha, self-possessed, however, pleased him during the months when he turned into a male, with stories full of righteous actions. (25)
m.uttara.90.2: On Śrī Rāma describing Purūravā’s wonderful birth, Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, the famous one, said again : ‘O best among men, please tell us what Ilā did after staying a year with the son of Soma (Budha).’ (1-2)
m.uttara.90.3: Hearing those sweet words of those two, Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, who eagerly asked him, Śrī Rāma again described the story of the son of Prajāpati, Ila. (3)
m.uttara.90.4: When Ila, had regained manhood for a month, the very wise one and possessed of fame, Budha, invited the very noble Saṁvarta Ṛṣi. (4)
m.uttara.90.5: He also invited Cyavana, the son of Bhṛgu, and the sage Ariṣṭanemi, the humorous Pramodana, Modakara and also the sage Durvāsā. (5)
m.uttara.90.6: Budha, skilled in conversation and truthful, addressed them all, who were friendly to him and were full of patience. (6)
m.uttara.90.7: That king of long arms is Ila, the son of Kardama : know what happened to him, do whatever is good for him here.’ (7)
m.uttara.90.8: While the Brāhmaṇas conversed with the sages, Kardama, the mighty one, came to that hermitage. (8)
m.uttara.90.9: Pulastya, Kratu and also Vaṣaṭkāra, Oṁkāra, the mighty one, too entered the hermitage. (9)
m.uttara.90.10: All those, happy at meeting each other, desirous of doing good to the lord of Bāhlīka, then spoke separately. (10)
m.uttara.90.11: Kardama, on his part, said that was best for his son, ‘O Brāhmaṇas, listen to me, which shall be for the welfare of the King. (11)
m.uttara.90.12: ‘I do not see any other cure except the pleasure of Rudra with the bull as emblem and no sacrifice other than the Aśvamedha is dearer to Śiva, the noble one. (12)
m.uttara.90.13: ‘Therefore, all of us, bulls among Brāhmaṇas, will perform a Yajña for the sake of the king’. (13)
m.uttara.90.15: They (Brāhmaṇas) approved of that sacrifice indeed for the appeasement of God Rudra (Śiva). A Ṛṣi among kings, well-known as Marutta, destroyer of enemies, who was the pupil of Saṁvarta, made necessary arrangements for that sacrifice. A great sacrifice was performed close to the hermitage of Budha. (14-15)
m.uttara.90.17: The mighty Rudra was extremely pleased at the completion of the sacrifice. Śiva, the lord of Umā, pleased and happy, spoke to all of them in the presence of Ila: ‘O best among Brāhmaṇas, I am pleased by the horse-sacrifice performed with devotion. (16-17)
m.uttara.90.19: ‘What good and auspicious act may I do for the lord of Bāhlīka.’ On the lord of gods speaking thus, those Brāhmaṇas, well-composed, propitiated the lord of gods, Śiva, in a manner that Ilā may turn into a man’. Then pleased, the great lord Śiva granted to Ilā perpetual manhood again. (18-19)
m.uttara.90.22: ‘The powerful Śiva, having granted manhood to Ilā, disappeared; and the horse-sacrifice being completed and Hara having disappeared, all the farsighted Brāhmaṇas went away as they came. The king, Ila, leaving Bāhlīka established the famous and unequalled Pratiṣṭhāna in the central region; Śaśabindu too the conqueror of fortresses of enemies re-established Bāhlīka. (20—22)
m.uttara.90.23: ‘At Pratiṣṭhāna, the king, son of Prajāpati, the powerful one, Ila in time attained the world of Brahmā. (23)
m.uttara.90.24: The king, Purūravā, son of Ila, obtained Pratiṣṭhāna, such is the power of Aśvamedha, O bull among men, one who was formerly a woman, achieved manhood—all that was difficult to obtain.’ (24)
m.uttara.91.1: Having narrated to his brothers, Śrī Rāma, with unlimited splendour, again spoke these righteous words to Lakṣmaṇa: (1)
m.uttara.91.3: ‘O Lakṣmaṇa, after having brought together all the sages e.g., Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Jābāli, Kāśyapa, and all Brāhmaṇas belonging to all Pravaras (Ṛṣi ancestors) and proficient in the performance of the Aśvamedha and also consulting them, I shall let loose a horse, with auspicious marks, carefully.’ (2-3)
m.uttara.91.4: Hearing those words of the descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa of speedy gait, calling all Brāhmaṇas presented them to the scion of Raghu. (4)
m.uttara.91.5: Having seen him, who was like a god, and had adored their feet, they honoured Śrī Rāma, the invincible, with blessings. (5)
m.uttara.91.6: Then folding his hands in salutation, the scion of Raghu, spoke to the best Brāhmaṇas about Aśvamedha, full of righteousness. (6)
m.uttara.91.7: All those Brāhmaṇas too having heard (the intention) of Śrī Rāma paying obeisance to Mahādeva, the god with the bull as His emblem, spoke very high of Aśvamedha. (7)
m.uttara.91.8: Having heard the wonderful words of the leading Brāhmaṇas, related to the Aśvamedha, he was extremely pleased. (8)
m.uttara.91.10: Knowing their intention to perform that sacrifice, Śrī Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa : ‘O one of long arms, send for the noble Sugrīva, alongwith several great monkeys and other denizens of the forest, to enjoy this great ceremony; may welfare be with them. (9-10)
m.uttara.91.11: ‘May Vibhīṣaṇa, too, possessed of great power, come to the great sacrifice, Aśvamedha, accompanied by the Rākṣasas (demons) moving at will. (11)
m.uttara.91.12: ‘All those kings of great fortune, who are desirous of my welfare, will come soon with attendants to see the ground of Aśvamedha. (12)
m.uttara.91.14: ‘O Lakṣmaṇa, invite all those Brāhmaṇas, who have migrated to other countries, are devoted to righteousness, on the occasion of Aśvamedha. O one of long arms, invite the sages rich in penance, and all the Brāhmaṇas staying abroad together with their spouses. (13-14)
m.uttara.91.16: ‘So also call the dancers with symbols, the actors and other dancers, make the great sacrificial place to be ready. O one of long arms, in the Naimiṣa forest on the banks of the Gomatī, that Naimiṣa forest is extremely holy; may propitiatory rites for averting evil be performed on all sides. (15-16)
m.uttara.91.18: ‘O one of long arms, descendant of Raghu, may righteous persons in thousands be satisfied, seeing the great sacrifice, the best among rites, Aśvamedha. O knower of righteousness, do invite all people soon, they will return satisfied, well-fed and honoured in the proper manner. (17-18)
m.uttara.91.20: ‘O mighty one, Lakṣmaṇa, may hundred thousand carriers carry unbroken rice, and ten thousand of them carry sesame and beans, grains, pulses, black gram a little and salt; and in proportionate quantity, lubricants and fragrant materials. (19—20)
m.uttara.91.25: ‘May Bharata proceed carrying coins in many hundred millions of gold and silver, carefully. Many rows of mobile markets, all actors and dancers, cooks, many damsels possessed of eternal charm, may they accompany Bharata; the citizens, both young and aged ones, Brāhmaṇas in front leading the march, the labourers, carpenters, treasurers and knowers of Veda, all my mothers (Kaikeyī with Sumitrā and Kausalyā), the spouses of the princes (Bharata etc.) ‘the gold statue of my wife, Sītā, and the knowers of the consecration ceremony, may Bharata possessed of great fame proceed.’ (21—25)
m.uttara.91.26: The powerful, Śrī Rāma, possessed of great power ordered to be built many costly dwellings for the powerful kings, together with their attendants. (26)
m.uttara.91.27: He also ordered for the provision of food and drinks for the noble ones, who followed them (kings). Bharata then proceeded together with Śatrughna. (27)
m.uttara.91.28: The noble monkeys, together with Sugrīva and the select Brāhmaṇas, then served the food. (28)
m.uttara.91.29: Vibhīṣaṇa together with the Rākṣasas and many women, received with honour the noble Ṛṣis of great penances. (29)
m.uttara.92.1: Dispatching all objects for performance of Yajña, the elder brother of Bharata, Śrī Rāma, let loose a horse, mostly black (like the spotted deer), possessed of auspicious marks. (1)
m.uttara.92.2: Entrusting Lakṣmaṇa together with the priests to look after the horse, the scion of Kakutstha proceeded to Naimiṣa with his army. (2)
m.uttara.92.3: That one of long arms, Śrī Rāma, seeing the most wonderful place of performance of the sacrifice, Aśvamedha, was highly pleased and exclaimed: This indeed is auspicious.’ (3)
m.uttara.92.4: While Śrī Rāma was residing in Naimiṣa, all other kings brought presents for him, and He reciprocated their benevolence by honouring them. (4)
m.uttara.92.5: Food and drinks, clothes and all other requirements were provided for them. Bharata and Śatrughna were charged with the duty of honouring the kings. (5)
m.uttara.92.6: The noble monkeys alongwith Sugrīva then served scrupulously clean and purified food to Brāhmaṇas attentively. (6)
m.uttara.92.7: Vibhīṣaṇa with many ogres offered their services to the Ṛṣis rich in austerities. (7)
m.uttara.92.8: The mighty one, best of kings Śrī Rāma ordered to be built costly dwellings for the noble kings as also for their followers. (8)
m.uttara.92.9: Thus the Aśvamedha Yajña was well-begun; the ambulation of the horse, protected by Lakṣmaṇa, was commended well. (9)
m.uttara.92.18: In this manner the great sacrifice of the lion among kings, Śrī Rāma, was performed; in that horse-sacrifice undertaken by Śrī Rāma, the noble one, no other sound was heard excepting cries of “Go on distributing till the needy ones are satisfied.” In that grand sacrifice of the noble one, were given various articles of jellys and also sugar. The monkeys and Rākṣasas were seen distributing food among those who begged for food till words of satisfaction did not come out of their lips. There was no one unclean, poor or emaciated in that great horse-sacrifice of the king, surrounded by happy and well-nourished beings. Those noble ascetics, long-lived ones, who came there, could not recall a sacrifice of that type so enriched with fabulous gifts and donations, who felt satisfied with gifts of gold, indeed; he who desired wealth, received it and one wishing gems also received them; Heaps of silver, gold, gems and garments being distributed constantly was seen in that sacrifice; ‘we have not seen such a sacrifice performed formerly by Indra, Soma, Yama or Varuṇa, thus said the sages rich in austerities. At all corners, there stood monkeys and demons; they distributed liberally among the suppliants, who desired clothes, wealth and food. (10—18)
m.uttara.92.19: Such a sacrifice of the lion among kings, possessed of all merits, went on for more than a year unobstructed. (19)
m.uttara.93.1: While that most wonderful sacrifice was going on, the venerable sage Vālmīki with his pupils came there soon. (1)
m.uttara.93.3: Ṛṣi Vālmīki saw the divine and astounding sacrifice. Vālmīki got his hut raised in the vicinity of other cottages of seers. They were all wonderful to look at. A number of carts, full of food-grains, lovely roots and fruits, were provided near his hut, not far from the sacrificial ground. (2-3)
m.uttara.93.4: The self-controlled Vālmīki of great lustre was respected by the king, Śrī Rāma and other hermits and great souls staying there. (4)
m.uttara.93.5: Vālmīki addressed the two cheerful pupils thus; ‘Go and carefully sing the entire poem, Rāmāyaṇa, most joyfully. (5)
m.uttara.93.6: ‘Sing in the holy huts of sages, in the dwellings of Brāhmaṇas, on the by-ways and highways and also in the residences of the kings,” (6)
m.uttara.93.7: ‘At the entrance of the apartment of Śrī Rāma and also where the ritual is being performed, and specially before the priests, this poem is to be sung. (7)
m.uttara.93.8: ‘These tasty fruits of many varieties have grown on the tops of the mountains. Enjoying them again and again, sing the poem. (8)
m.uttara.93.9: ‘O you two, dear ones, having eaten the fruits and also the roots well-ruled, you shall not tire and not deviate from the Rāga (musical notes). (9)
m.uttara.93.10: ‘If Śrī Rāma calls you to hear your song, then perform the singing of the poem in front of the sages seated, to the best of your ability. (10)
m.uttara.93.11: ‘Twenty cantoes are to be sung in a day in a melodious voice, as instructed by me with different number of verses as instructed by me earlier. (11)
m.uttara.93.12: ‘Do not be greedy even in the least with desire for wealth; of what use is wealth to dwellers of hermitages and subsisting always on fruits and roots? (12)
m.uttara.93.13: ‘If that scion of Kakutstha asks you: “whose sons are you two, then say to the king thus “We are the two disciples of Vālmīki”. (13)
m.uttara.93.14: ‘Playing on these lutes, emitting sweet sounds, and wonderfully divided according to musical notes, sing sweetly, having no worry. (14)
m.uttara.93.15: ‘This Rāmāyaṇa has to be sung from the beginning; do nothing disrespectful to the king; the king is the father of all beings, according to the law. (15)
m.uttara.93.16: ‘Therefore, you two, with a cheerful mind and attentively sing tomorrow morning the sweet song, accompanied with the lute and keeping proper tune and rhythm. (16)
m.uttara.93.17: Having thus instructed many times, the son of Pracetā, the great sage Vālmīki, the most large-hearted one, then became silent. (17)
m.uttara.93.18: Thus instructed by that sage, both those two sons of Maithilī (Sītā), the subduer of foes, saying ‘we shall do as you say’ went out. (18)
m.uttara.93.19: Then keeping the wonderful words of the sage Vālmīki, the two young children, Lava and Kuśa, eager to sing slept with ease like the two Aśwanīkumāras having learnt the teachings of Śukra. (19)
m.uttara.94.2: As the night passed and the day approached, both Kuśa and Lava having taken their bath and made offerings to the fire, sang the poem there, as instructed by the sage Vālmīki. That scion of Kakutstha heard that musical recitation accompanied with musical notes, unheard of before, composed as per the cadences set by former great masters of music. (1-2)
m.uttara.94.3: The descendant of Raghu, Śrī Rāma, hearing that song, set to the proper time and tune and accompanied by the playing of the lute by the two boys, was amazed. (3)
m.uttara.94.10: Then in the midst of the performance of the Aśvamedha Yajña, the king, Śrī Rāma, the tiger among men, having called, the great ascetics, the other kings and the learned citizens, the specialists in the Purāṇas, and also those aged Brāhmaṇas who were proficient in the knowledge of words, and also those best among Brāhmaṇas, who were curious to hear the Rāmāyaṇa and knew the specialities of musical notes, the knowers of auspicious marks, the musicians, all citizens, the knowers of the relation between the syllables of stanza and were proficient in metres; those who excelled in art only, and those well-versed in astrology, knowers of ritual performances, and also those specializing in the details of the ritual and those skilled in suggesting remedial forms of ritual, the logicians and also the erudite ones, the verifiers and knowers of the Purāṇas, the Vedas, the best among Brāhmaṇas, knowers of the Citra (forms of the Kāvya), knowers of the Sūtras on righteous conduct (Dharmasūtras) and also experts in vocal music and dance, and bringing all of them together, made the two singers sit in the assembly of all these. (4—10)
m.uttara.94.11: Those two sons of the sage (Lava and Kuśa) then started singing, causing more joy to audience who were talking among themselves. (11)
m.uttara.94.12: Then continued the super-human music; all hearing it were not satiated by its musical culture and desired to hear more of it. (12)
m.uttara.94.13: The hosts of sages were in joy and also the mighty kings, seeing again and again the two boys as if they would drink them up through their eyes. (13)
m.uttara.94.14: They looked attentively and said to each other: ‘Both are similar to Śrī Rāma as a reflection of the original object. (14)
m.uttara.94.15: ‘If they were not bearing matted hair or not dressed in bark-garments, we could not differentiate between those two singers and the descendant of Raghu, the king, Śrī Rāma. (15)
m.uttara.94.16: While the citizens and townsmen talked in this way, the first canto attributed to Nārada was sung from the beginning. (16)
m.uttara.94.19: From then on, they sang till the twenty cantos were completed. Then in the evening Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, affectionate to his brothers after hearing the twenty cantos, spoke to his brother: “Give to these two noble ones soon, eighteen thousand gold coins, and whatever else they ask for.” The scion of Kakutstha, Bharata, at once began to give it to those two boys separately. (17—19)
m.uttara.94.20: The two—Kuśa and Lava, the noble ones, did not accept the gold coins being given to them and they said in surprise: ‘Of what use are these to us.’ (20)
m.uttara.94.21: ‘We reside in the forest and subsist daily on fruits and roots. What shall we do with gold and silver coins in the forest.’ (21)
m.uttara.94.22: Thus as both of them spoke, those who heard them together with Śrī Rāma, too, were surprised and filled with curiosity. (22)
m.uttara.94.23: Desirous to know the composer of that poem, Śrī Rāma, the mighty one, asked both of those two ascetics: (23)
m.uttara.94.24: “How long is this poem? What is the object of the noble one, Vālmīki? Where is the composer of this poem, the best among ascetics.” (24)
m.uttara.94.25: The two sons of ascetic said to the scion of Raghu, ‘The venerable sage Vālmīki is the composer who has come to this place of performance. By this poem he has revealed the whole life’s account to you. (25)
m.uttara.94.26: ‘Twenty-four thousand Ślokas (verses) with a hundred legends have been composed by the ascetic, Bhārgava Vālmīki, the brother of Bhṛgu. (26)
m.uttara.94.28: ‘From the beginning, O King, five hundred cantos with six Kāṇḍas (parts) together with the Uttara (best Kāṇḍa) have been composed by the noble one, our preceptor, sage Vālmīki, keeping in mind your life’s deeds which will continue till all beings live. (27-28)
m.uttara.94.29: ‘O king, the great chariot-warrior, if you have a mind to hear it, then in between this performance of Yajña, listen joyfully together with your brothers.’ (29)
m.uttara.94.30: “Be it so” said Śrī Rāma, and the two taking leave (of Śrī Rāma), went cheerfully to the place where the great sage was staying. (30)
m.uttara.94.31: Śrī Rāma too with the ascetics and the noble kings, having heard the sweet song, approached the place of performance. (31)
m.uttara.94.32: The song set into Chandas with proper words, embettered by proper beats and time, sung by Kuśa and Lava with lute in harmony, was heard by the scion of the Kakutsthas, Śrī Rāma. (32)
m.uttara.95.1: For many days Śrī Rāma, together with the ascetics, kings and monkeys, heard that wonderful song of holy content. (1)
m.uttara.95.2: Having known through that song, Lava and Kuśa as the sons of Sītā, Śrī Rāma spoke in that assembly of sages, kings and monkeys. (2)
m.uttara.95.3: Having called envoys of pure conduct, and contemplating inwardly, said to them: “Go to the venerable Ṛṣi Vālmīki and convey to him my words ! (3)
m.uttara.95.4: “If she (Sītā) is pure of conduct, if any of the sins do not dwell in her, then may she prove her purity here at the bidding of the great sage Vālmīki. (4)
m.uttara.95.5: “Having known the wish of the sage and Sītā’s willingness to give proof of her purity, let me know at once. (5)
m.uttara.95.6: “Let Maithilī (Sītā), the daughter of Janaka, take oath in front of this assembly to remove blemishes from me also tomorrow morning.” (6)
m.uttara.95.7: Hearing these wonderful words of Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, envoys nodding ascent, went to the place where the great sage Vālmīki stayed. (7)
m.uttara.95.8: Having saluted the noble one of inimitable lustre and resplendent, they spoke the words of Śrī Rāma, soft and sweet. (8)
m.uttara.95.9: Having heard their words, and knowing the intention of Śrī Rāma, the very powerful sage spoke thus: (9)
m.uttara.95.10: “So be it, welfare be with you, Sītā will do as desired by Śrī Rāma, as husband is indeed a god for the wife.” (10)
m.uttara.95.11: Thus spoken to by the sage, all the royal envoys, coming back, repeated all that the sage had said, to mighty Rāma. (11)
m.uttara.95.12: Then Śrī Rāma, the scion of Kakutstha, highly pleased on hearing the words of Vālmīki, the noble one, addressed the sages and also the kings assembled there: (12)
m.uttara.95.13: ‘Venerable sages, with pupils and kings with attendants or anyone else, so desiring, may witness the oath-taking of Sītā. (13)
m.uttara.95.14: Hearing those words of the noble descendant of Raghu, all the chief sages exclaimed ‘well done.’ (14)
m.uttara.95.15: The noble kings praised indeed the descendant of Raghu thus: ‘O best among men, this behoves you only, and no one else.’ (15)
m.uttara.95.16: Thus deciding that the oath-taking shall take place tomorrow, then the descendant of Raghu, the extirpator of foes, discharged the assembly. (16)
m.uttara.95.17: That lion among kings, the great and magnanimous one, deciding the oath to take place next day, allowed all noble ones to leave. (17)
m.uttara.96.7: As the night passed, the King, Śrī Rāma, the powerful one, going to the place of sacrifice, reckoned all the sages—Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, Jābāli and Kāśyapa, Viśvāmitra, Dīrghatamā, the great ascetic Durvāsā, also Pulastya and Śakti, Bhārgava, Vāmana, Markaṇḍeya the long-lived one, the famous Maudgalya, Garga, Cyavana, the religious Śatānanda, the splendrous Bharadvāja, the son of Agni, the lustrous one, Nārada, Parvata, the most famous Gautama all these sages and other ascetics of austere vows, filled with curiosity, came, and also the most powerful Rākṣasas and monkeys. (1—7)
m.uttara.96.8: All Kṣatriyas and Śūdras, and thousands of Vaiśyas, noble ones, came out of curiosity. (8)
m.uttara.96.9: Brāhmaṇas coming from all places, well-versed in vows came to witness the oath-taking of Sītā. (9)
m.uttara.96.10: Then coming to know that all those who came were rendered motionless as stone, the great sage Vālmīki came soon after, accompanied by Sītā. (10)
m.uttara.96.11: Sītā followed the sage, with face downcast and hands folded, inarticulate due to tears, keeping Śrī Rāma in the heart. (11)
m.uttara.96.12: Seeing Sītā approaching after Vālmīki as the Śruti (Vedas) follows Brahmā (creator). There was great uproar of appreciation. (12)
m.uttara.96.13: Then the sound of Halahalā (sighs of sorrow) arose among all those who were agitated by great sorrow arising out of suffering. (13)
m.uttara.96.14: Some said: ‘Well done’ Śrī Rāma, while others said: ‘Well done’ Śrī Sītā. There all observers praised both of them, Śrī Rāma and Śrī Sītā. (14)
m.uttara.96.15: Then in the midst of that assembly of men the great sage entering, accompanied by Sītā, spoke thus to the descendant of Raghu: (15)
m.uttara.96.16: ‘O son of Daśaratha, this pious Sītā of righteous conduct was left by you near my hermitage out of fear of censure by folks. (16)
m.uttara.96.17: ‘O Rāma, possessed of great vows, Sītā will give assurance of her good conduct before you as you are afraid of public censure, please permit her to do so. (17)
m.uttara.96.18: ‘These twin sons of Sītā are indeed your sons, difficult to conquer by foes, this is the truth, I tell you. (18)
m.uttara.96.19: ‘O descendant of Raghu, I am the tenth son of Pracetā (Varuṇa). I do not remember having spoken untruth. These twins are verily your sons. (19)
m.uttara.96.20: ‘I have practised penances for many thousand years—may I not obtain the fruits thereof, if Maithilī (Sītā) is wicked of conduct. (20)
m.uttara.96.21: ‘No sin has been committed by me in my earlier life through mind, speech or action; may I gain the fruit of this sinless conduct if Sītā is sinless. (21)
m.uttara.96.22: ‘Rāghava, through deep meditation I came to the conclusion that all ingredients like five gross elements and mind etc., subtle elements in Sītā are in their purest form. And it is only then that I took her from the bank of the river in the forest to my hermitage. (22)
m.uttara.96.23: ‘This sinless, pure of conduct, Sītā, looking upon her husband as the only god, shall give assurance to you, afraid as you are of censure by public. (23)
m.uttara.96.24: ‘Therefore, this one O! son of king Daśaratha, forsakan by you for fear of public censure, I have known her through divine vision to be of pure conduct and devoted to you even though you already knew that she was chaste.’ (24)
m.uttara.97.1: Thus spoken to by Vālmīki, the scion of Raghu, replied with folded hands, seeing the beautiful complexioned one, Sītā, within the sight of everybody: (1)
m.uttara.97.2: ‘O holy one, this is as you say, O knower of law, O Brāhmaṇa, by your guiltless words, I am assured. (2)
m.uttara.97.3: ‘Sītā, the daughter of Videha, has already assured us of her pure conduct in front of the gods, and taken oath and then she was allowed to enter the apartment. (3)
m.uttara.97.4: ‘The censure by people is great, due to which Maithilī (Sītā) was forsaken. This Sītā, O Brāhmaṇa, was forsaken by me due to fear of censure, although knowing that she was sinless, so please forgive me. (4)
m.uttara.97.5: ‘I know these two are my sons, the twins, Kuśa and Lava, and yet let her chastity be acknowledged by the world and my love in her reinstated.’ (5)
m.uttara.97.6: Knowing the intention of Śrī Rāma, the great gods, all of them came in connection with the oath-taking of Sītā. (6)
m.uttara.97.8: Having Brahmā at their head, the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvadevas, the hosts of Maruts, all the Sādhya gods, all great sages, the Nāgas, Suparṇas and the Siddhas, all came joyfully. (7-8)
m.uttara.97.9: Seeing all the gods and sages, who came out of respect for the scion of Raghu, again said: ‘O best among men, my faith is gained by the guiltless words of the sage, Vālmīki’. (9)
m.uttara.97.10: ‘May my love for Sītā, sinless in the eyes of all, be all out.’ (10)
m.uttara.97.11: Then the holy and pure wind-god blew emitting divine fragrance, caused joy to all on all sides. (11)
m.uttara.97.12: That wonderful and unconceivable happening as used to be in Kṛtayuga was seen by all men coming from various countries. (12)
m.uttara.97.13: Sītā wearing a brown garment, having seen all of them arrived, with folded hands, keeping her gaze downwards and face cast down, said: (13)
m.uttara.97.14: ‘As I have not contemplated about anyone other than the scion of Raghu even in mind, so the goddess Mādhavī, the earth-goddess, may provide space to me to enter. (14)
m.uttara.97.15: ‘As I worship Śrī Rāma, in mind, speech and action, so the spouse of Mādhava (the earth-goddess Mādhavī) may grant space to me to enter. (15)
m.uttara.97.16: ‘As I have spoken the truth that I do not know anyone except Śrī Rāma, so the earth-goddess may grant space to me.’ (16)
m.uttara.97.18: Then, while Sītā, the daughter of Videha, was taking oath, a divine throne, of wonderful beauty arose from the earth, borne on the head by very powerful Nāgas (serpents) adorned with divine ornaments, and looking divine in form sprang up. (17-18)
m.uttara.97.19: On that throne, the earth-goddess, welcoming her with words of welcome, and taking her by her hands made Sītā be seated on the seat. (19)
m.uttara.97.20: Seeing Sītā thus seated, entering the netherworld, a divine shower of flowers in succession covered Sītā. (20)
m.uttara.97.22: All of a sudden loud shouts of ‘well-done’ arose from the gods “Well done,” Well done, O Sītā, who are of such conduct’— thus and other words of approbation were uttered by the gods, happy in mind seeing Sītā’s entry into the netherworld. (21-22)
m.uttara.97.23: All ascetics and kings, tigers among men, that had come to the place of great event, continued to acclaim Sītā out of amazement. (23)
m.uttara.97.24: In the firmament, on earth all movable and stationary beings, the mighty sons of Danu (devils) and overlords of serpents acclaimed. (24)
m.uttara.97.25: Some uttered hurrahs of joy, other fixed their gaze on Sītā, while others looked at Śrī Rāma, although in meditation. (25)
m.uttara.97.26: All had assembled to witness the submersion of Sītā into the netherworld; that moment all the world was as if stupefied. (26)
m.uttara.98.1: When Sītā had entered the netherworld, all the monkeys and the ascetics exclaimed ‘well-done’ in the presence of Śrī Rāma. (1)
m.uttara.98.2: Propping himself on the wooden stick, with his eyes afflicted by tears, head downcast in mental agony, Śrī Rāma was indeed very much grieved. (2)
m.uttara.98.3: Weeping long and shedding tears in profusion, possessed of both anger and sorrow, he said: (3)
m.uttara.98.4: ‘A sorrow unexperienced before, is about to overpower mind as Sītā the goddess of wealth—incarnate disappeared just before my eyes. (4)
m.uttara.98.5: Sītā disappeared formerly, being carried to Laṅkā across the ocean; I brought her back from there; what to say of bringing her back from the Earth. He spoke: (5)
m.uttara.98.6: ‘O goddess of Earth, venerable one, please return to me Sītā or else I shall show my anger as you know me (my might). (6)
m.uttara.98.7: ‘You indeed are my mother-in-law; Maithilī (Sītā) was taken out of you formerly by Janaka while ploughing field with a golden plough. (7)
m.uttara.98.8: ‘Therefore, either return Sītā or else grant space to me. I will stay with her in the netherworld or in heaven. (8)
m.uttara.98.10: ‘Please bring that Sītā; I have gone mad for her; if you will not give back to me Sītā as she was on this earth, I shall put you to ruin, with the mountains and forests ruined entirely; I shall destroy the whole earth—may the waters flood over the entire earth.’ (9-10)
m.uttara.98.11: On being thus spoken by the scion of Kākutstha, overtaken by anger and sorrow, Brahmā together with the gods spoke to the descendant of Raghu: (11)
m.uttara.98.12: ‘O Rāma, O Śrī Rāma, possessor of good vows, please do not be grieved, recall your previous form and advice to the gods, O destroyer of foes. (12)
m.uttara.98.13: ‘I do not dare remind you of your former form, O one of long arms, but pray to you to remember at this moment, O one, difficult to conquer, your incarnation pertaining to Viṣṇu. (13)
m.uttara.98.14: ‘The pure and noble Sītā, devoted to yourself as before, has gone to the netherworld (Nāgaloka both netherworld and also the world of Viṣṇu) by the power of penances in the form of complete surrender to you. (14)
m.uttara.98.15: ‘Your union with her will again take place in heaven, listen to what I say in the midst of this assembly. (15)
m.uttara.98.16: ‘This poem, Rāmāyaṇa, dedicated to you, that you have heard is the best among all poems, O Rāma; it shall describe everything in detail, there is no doubt. (16)
m.uttara.98.17: ‘In this poem all has been described by Vālmīki, all happiness and sorrow that you have experienced from your birth, and also what you will experience in future. (17)
m.uttara.98.18: ‘This first and foremost poem, O Rāma, is entirely based on you. No one other than you will be possessed of fame to be described as hero by the poem. (18)
m.uttara.98.19: ‘I have heard all this formerly, together with the gods, all wonderful and possessed of true statements with nothing concealed. (19)
m.uttara.98.20: ‘So you, O lion among men, scion of Kākutsthas should carefully listen to the remaining portion of the poem, Rāmāyaṇa dealing with happenings of the future. (20)
m.uttara.98.21: ‘The remaining part of this poem, O famous one, is known as Uttarakāṇḍa; O powerful one, listen to it, possessed of excellence, with the sages. (21)
m.uttara.98.22: O Scion of Kākutstha, this best portion is indeed not to be heard by anyone else, composed by the great great sage, O brave, it is to be heard only by you.’ (22)
m.uttara.98.23: Having spoken this much, Brahmā, the lord of the three worlds, went to heaven together with other gods. (23)
m.uttara.98.28: The noble and splendrous sages belonging to the world of Brahmā, being ordered by Brahmā, returned, having a mind to hear what will happen to the scion of Raghu thereafter in the future. Then the most powerful Śrī Rāma after hearing the holy words spoken by the God of gods, Brahmā, said to Vālmīki: ‘Sir the Uttarakāṇḍa pertaining to what will happen to me in future, that the sages of the world of Brahmā desire to hear, may be described tomorrow.’ Thus having decided, taking hold to Kuśa and Lava, He (Śrī Rāma) leaving that assembly of men, went to his arbour—and as he kept thinking of Sītā, that night passed. (24—28)
m.uttara.99.1: After the night had passed, dawn came, Rāma said to the two sons, calling all the great sages, “Sing unhesitatingly”. (1)
m.uttara.99.2: Then after the great and noble sages had taken their seats, the twin Kuśa and Lava sang the poem relating to the Uttarakāṇḍa, dealing with events of the future: (2)
m.uttara.99.4: “On Sītā entering the netherworld through the efficacy of truth, Śrī Rāma was much agitated at the conclusion of the sacrifice and considered this earth as a void. Not being able to see Sītā and being terribly afflicted by sorrow, he had no peace of mind. (3-4)
m.uttara.99.7: Leaving all kings, the bears and monkeys, and also the great assembly of the chief Brāhmaṇas, giving them precious gifts, Lotus-eyed Rāma, after finishing the sacrifice, alongwith his two sons, Sītā in his heart, entered Ayodhyā. (5—7)
m.uttara.99.8: That descendant of Raghu did not take as wife any one other than Sītā and at every sacrifice (Aśvamedha) the gold image of the daughter of Janaka served as the queen. (8)
m.uttara.99.9: Then He, Śrī Rāma, performed horse-sacrifices and Vājapeya sacrifices ten times that number, full with the distribution of gold coins, for ten thousand years. (9)
m.uttara.99.10: That prosperous one, Śrī Rāma, performed many Gosavas with the Agniṣṭoma and the Atirātra and also other sacrifices, giving donations in plenty. (10)
m.uttara.99.11: Thus that period of Śrī Rāma elapsed, the descendant of Raghu, acting righteously, ruling over His Kingdom. (11)
m.uttara.99.12: The bears, monkeys and demons obeyed the command of the descendant of Raghu, the Kings paid tributes to Him day by day. (12)
m.uttara.99.13: The clouds rained timely, the harvest was good and the quarters shone clearly, and the towns and cities were full of happy, well-fed and healthy persons in His reign. (13)
m.uttara.99.14: No one died prematurely, no physical ailment was suffered by living beings, no calamity took place as Śrī Rāma ruled over his Kingdom. (14)
m.uttara.99.15: After a long lapse of time the mother of Rāma, Kausalyā of great fame, surrounded by her son and grandsons, succumbed to the law of time. (15)
m.uttara.99.16: Sumitrā and the Kaikeyī also followed her, performing various charitable deeds, and praiseworthy, were established in heaven. (16)
m.uttara.99.17: All happy and righteous ones, united with Daśaratha in heaven, attained the fruit of all religious performances. (17)
m.uttara.99.18: Śrī Rāma made great donations for his mothers, Kausalyā, Kaikeyī, Sumitrā, without any difference, to the Brāhmaṇa ascetics. (18)
m.uttara.99.19: Śrī Rāma, the noble one, donated the most cherished things to Brāhmaṇas and performed the sacrifices most difficult to accomplish, to add to the glory of his ancestors and the gods. (19)
m.uttara.99.20: Many a thousand years passed while Śrī Rāma upraised the course of Dharma (religion) by performing various sacrifices. (20)
m.uttara.100.3: After some time, the King of Kekaya, Yudhājit, sent his preceptor, Brāhmaṇa Gārgya, the son of Aṅgirā, possessed of inimitable lustre to Śrī Rāma, the noble descendant of Raghu. The King presented a §gift of ten thousand horses as a token of affection and also blankets and precious gems, and garments of various kinds and brilliant ornaments. (1—3)
m.uttara.100.5: Having heard that the great sage Gārgya had come, bringing with him the rich gifts sent by the maternal uncle, Aśvapati, Śrī Rama, alongwith his brothers, welcomed Gārgya at a distance of two miles in advance, and honoured Gārgya as Indra honours Bṛhaspati. (4-5)
m.uttara.100.13: Thus having honoured that sage and accepting the gifts, he enquired of the welfare of his maternal uncle. Śrī Rāma asked the holy one when he had seated himself thus: ‘What has my maternal uncle said for which O Venerable Sir, best among the knowers of Śāstras, like Bṛhaspti himself, you have come.’ Having heard the words of Śrī Rāma, the great sage began to speak in detail the wondrous purpose to the descendant of Raghu: ‘O one of long arms, bull among men, your maternal uncle Yudhājit has said pleasingly, listen if it appeals to you. The territory of the Gandharvas, rich with fruits and roots, is a region most beautiful on both sides of the Sindhu river, that is protected by the Gandharvas, the experts in war, possessed of arms, the powerful three million sons of Śailūṣa, O brave one. Having conquered them, O scion of Kakutstha, merge the holy city of the Gandharvas in your own kingdom, which no one else can do. May it please you to occupy it, O one of long arms; I do not say this against your interests.’ (6—13)
m.uttara.100.14: Having heard this, Śrī Rāma the descendant of Raghu, being pleased with what the sage and his maternal uncle said: ‘So shall it be’ and looked at Bharata. (14)
m.uttara.100.16: That descendant of Raghu was pleased and with folded hands courteously said: ‘O Ṛṣi among Brāhmaṇas, these two brave sons (of Bharata) Takṣa and Puṣkala will go to that region, well-protected by my maternal uncle and observing religious norms. (15-16)
m.uttara.100.17: ‘Keeping Bharata ahead, the two sons together with their army and attendants, will divide the two regions having killed the sons of the Gandharva, Śailūṣa. (17)
m.uttara.100.18: ‘Establishing those two cities and foresetting his two sons there, this most pious one, Bharata, will again return to me.’ (18)
m.uttara.100.20: Thus having spoken to the Brāhmaṇas, he (Rāma) ordered Bharata to proceed with his army and attendants, and also consecrated the two sons on an auspicious day with the holy star, putting the son of Aṅgirā at their head, Bharata with his army and his sons proceeded. (19-20)
m.uttara.100.21: Then that army went out of the royal city Ayodhyā like the army of Indra, followed by the descendant of Raghu for a long distance—the army that was difficult to conquer even by the gods. (21)
m.uttara.100.22: The flesh-eaters and the mighty Rākṣasas followed Bharata out of thirst for blood. (22)
m.uttara.100.23: Hosts of Bhūtas (demons), eaters of flesh, the terrible ones, desirous of devouring the flesh of the sons of the Gandharva, followed in thousands. (23)
m.uttara.100.24: Lions, tigers, bears and the sky-roving birds, thousands in number went to herald the army. (24)
m.uttara.100.25: Having spent one and half months on the way, the army, hale and hearty, bearing happy and well-fed men, reached Kekaya territory. (25)
m.uttara.101.1: Yudhājit, the king of Kekaya, having heard of the arrival of Bharata as the Commander-in-chief of his army, was highly pleased together with Gārgya. (1)
m.uttara.101.2: He, the lord of Kekaya, and Bharata set out accompanied by a large army and quickly reached the capital of the Gandharvas. (2)
m.uttara.101.3: Bharata and Yudhājit accompanied by the rapid action warriors reached the city of Gandharvas with the army and attendants. (3)
m.uttara.101.4: Those Gandharvas, possessed of great power, and desirous of war came out, shouting war cries every where. (4)
m.uttara.101.5: Then there ensued a great battle enough to cause horripilation for seven nights in a terrible form, and yet none came out victorious. (5)
m.uttara.101.6: Rivers with streams of blood, having crocodiles in the form of swords, arrows and bows, and carrying the corpses of men, gushed forth on all sides. (6)
m.uttara.101.7: Then Bharata, the brother of Śrī Rāma, highly enraged directed the most terrible weapon of death, Saṁvarta by name, towards the Gandharvas. (7)
m.uttara.101.8: Struck by the mighty Saṁvarta, as if bound by the noose of death, they the Gandharvas, three million in number, perished in a moment. (8)
m.uttara.101.9: Even the gods did not remember a battle so fierce in which those mighty Gandharvas were killed in a moment. (9)
m.uttara.101.11: On all of the Gandharvas being killed, Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, founded there two great and prosperous cities and he installed Takṣa on Takṣaśilā in the Gandharva-Deśa and Puṣkala on Puṣkalāvata in the territory of Gāndhāras. (10-11)
m.uttara.101.16: Having fully established the two above— named cities, filled with wealth and gems, beautified by gardens, trying each other to excel through competitive spirit, both extremely lovely and rich with fresh business, abounding in pleasant groves and carrier vehicles and well-planned with markets, both great cities, beautifully decorated with mansions and many lovely Vimānas (palaces), adorned with attractive temples of worship, made lovely with the Tālas, Tamālas, Tilaka and Vakula trees. In five years, Bharata the younger brother of Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Raghus, possessed of long arms, the son of Kaikeyī, returned to Ayodhyā. (12—16)
m.uttara.101.18: Having bowed to Śrī Rāma, the noble descendant of Raghu, who was as if he were another Dharma (Law)—incarnate, as Indra bows to Brahmā, the graceful Bharata narrated to him how the great battle with the Gandharvas was fought and how were founded the two cities, too. Hearing him, Śrī Rāma, the descendant of Raghu, was highly pleased. (17-18)
m.uttara.102.1: Hearing this account of Bharata, Śrī Rāma, together with his brothers, was pleased and said to Lakṣmaṇa these words of wonderful content: (1)
m.uttara.102.2: ‘O son of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, your these two sons are knower of Dharma (Law and righteousness)—named Aṅgada and Candraketu, possessed of firm fortitude, for the protection of their kingdoms. (2)
m.uttara.102.3: ‘I shall consecrate these two, find out a suitable region, that is enjoyable and where the two archers may remain happily without being obstructed. (3)
m.uttara.102.4: ‘O gracious one, find out that place, where the kings are not tormented and the hermitages are well-protected and we may not be at fault later on.’ (4)
m.uttara.102.6: On Śrī Rāma saying thus, Bharata replied: ‘This region known as Kārupatha is indeed beautiful and free from all ills. Establish there the city under the noble Aṅgada and also a region known as Candrakānta free from sorrow, for Candraketu, the noble one.’ (5-6)
m.uttara.102.7: This statement of Bharata was accepted by Śrī Rāma, descendant of Raghu and having brought that territory Kārupatha under him, he established the city there for Aṅgada. (7)
m.uttara.102.8: The city that was bestowed by Śrī Rāma on Aṅgada was beautiful indeed and well-protected on all sides. (8)
m.uttara.102.9: For the wrestler Candraketu, the city well-known as Candrakāntā in Malla country was established as the divine city in heaven. (9)
m.uttara.102.10: Then Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Bharata, all difficult to conquer in war, were highly pleased and performed the coronation of Aṅgada and Candraketu. (10)
m.uttara.102.11: Having consecrated and sent Aṅgada to the western region and Candraketu northwards, both firm in mind, they were well pleased. (11)
m.uttara.102.12: Lakṣmaṇa, the son of Sumitrā, too, followed Aṅgada and Bharata on his part followed Candraketu as the rear guard. (12)
m.uttara.102.13: Having stayed for one full year in the city of Aṅgada, when his son, difficult to conquer was well-established, Lakṣmaṇa came back again to Ayodhyā. (13)
m.uttara.102.14: Bharata too, having spent a year and more, in the same manner returned to Ayodhyā and worshipped the feet of Śrī Rāma. (14)
m.uttara.102.15: Both—the son of Sumitrā (Lakṣmaṇa) and Bharata, the most noble ones, ardently attached to the feet of Śrī Rāma, were oblivious of the lapse of time due to the deep affection of Śrī Rāma. (15)
m.uttara.102.16: Thus, ten thousand years passed with Śrī Rāma, Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa striving always to perform tasks for the citizens and always ready to follow Dharma. (16)
m.uttara.102.17: With desires all fulfilled, established in the city of virtue, full of prosperity, the three brothers radiated effulgence like the three great sacrificial fires, inflamed by oblations well poured. (17)
m.uttara.103.1: After sometime, while Śrī Rāma was engaged in virtuous deeds, Death in the form of an ascetic appeared at the royal gate. (1)
m.uttara.103.2: He spoke to courageous and glorious Lakṣmaṇa, who was standing at the door thus: ‘I have come here for a great purpose, you report my arrival to Śrī Rāma. (2)
m.uttara.103.3: ‘I am the messenger of the sage Atibala, possessed of great power and have come desiring to see Śrī Rāma with a purpose, O mighty one.’ (3)
m.uttara.103.4: Having heard the words of the ascetic, the son of Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, at once reported the arrival of that ascetic to Śrī Rāma ! (4)
m.uttara.103.5: ‘O one possessed of great power, be victorious over both the worlds: a messenger, who is as lustrous as the sun, due to austerities, has come to see you.’ (5)
m.uttara.103.6: Śrī Rāma on his part hearing the words of Lakṣmaṇa said: ‘O dear, let the messenger possessed of great vigour, who carries the message of his patron, enter.’ (6)
